**THE DECISIONS TO SEE FIRST (for the orchestrator and the owner).**

1. **THE SPEC'S "A MINION'S BODY IS NOT GROUND" GATE IS REVERSED BY THE LISTING, AND WAS NOT BUILT AS WRITTEN.** The backlog row (G10-3, from step 148) said the original's feet "refuse a character" and read it as a minion. `shouldBeIgnoredByFeet` (bytes 361584..361843) refuses a sensor, `isCharacter`, `fireball.ent` and a name beginning `anti_sight_wall`, and nothing else; `isCharacter` is set only by `GameCharacter::GameCharacter` (ins 43-56), which only `SideScrollerCharacter` (ins 34) and so `MainCharacter` (ins 35) construct - the listing has one `ALLOC` each, no `.ent` carries the datum, no converted level sets it (`grep isCharacter out/levels/*.tscn`: none), and a minion is `AddEntity('minion.ent')` (`spawnMinion`, ins 39), `sensor="0"`. **The only character is the player**, and the refusal is of his own body (the feet's sensor touches the capsule it is moved to). So a minion's or a knight's body, a crate, a stone, a barrel, a platform and a lift all hold him, as the port already had them (`Grounded` excluded only the player). The rulings say the original wins, so the suite pins `AMinionsBodyIsGroundAsACrateAndAPlatformAre` the other way round (a synthetic minion-sized sphere is ground, and a real minion of 1-04's level, `level0b`, holds the feet and stops doing so when its collider is taken away); step 148's deviation 3 now carries a pointer to this step and `Player.hpp`'s comment is corrected. The real G10-3 work was the audit of what the feet refuse: ten `.ent` files say `sensor="1"`, the 128 converted levels place six names of them 90 times and **every one is an `Area2D`** (a trigger the sensor never sees); `fireball.ent` has no body in the port. Pinned by `NoSensorOfTheOriginalIsBuiltAsASolidBody`.
2. **THE CAPSULE IS THE HULL OF THE TWO CIRCLES; THE ORIGINAL'S WAIST IS FILLED** (deviation 1). The engine has one collider per entity and no compound, so the original's two circles of radius 9.1 at +-9 are built as their hull, a capsule 18.2 wide and 36.2 tall, which has the circles' own extreme points, cap centres and radius. Their union is 2.69 units wide at the waist where the capsule is 18.2: a corner at the player's waist can nest in the original's notch up to 7.75 units and cannot here.
3. **THE PLAYER AT REST STANDS 1.7-1.8 PX LOWER THAN THE LIBRARY STILLS' ON A FLOOR, AND THE CAUSE IS THE ENGINE'S CONTACT SKIN, NOT THE CAPSULE** (deviation 2). Before: the sprite stood 9.1 to 9.4 px HIGHER than the original's on 13 flat-floor levels (the Godot 44-tall capsule rests its centre 22 over the floor less the engine's skin, the original's 18.35). After: +1.7 to +1.8 px lower (13 flat-floor levels, 1-01 to 1-32: before -9.19 px on average, -9.38 to -9.09; after +1.75, +1.53 to +1.86). Box2D rests a circle on a polygon 0.25 units ABOVE its surface (`b2_polygonRadius` 0.01 m less `b2_linearSlop` 0.005 m, `b2ContactSolver.cpp:712`); the Supersonic solver rests the capsule 0.46 units INTO a floor (0.55 into the ramp, 0.73 into a small crate: `test_mp_player` prints them), 0.71 together - the measured residual. It is every body's (a crate on a floor rests 0.75 above it in Box2D and 0.46 into it here), so a picture lift for the player alone would put him 0.6 units high in flight and leave the crates; the engine has no contact-margin setting. Left as an engine row (LEFT FOR THE OWNER).
4. **G10-6 IS BUILT AT THE SCREEN'S OWN 100 PIXELS, AND THE SIM LEARNS THE SCREEN FROM THE LAYER ONLY.** `b2_maxTranslation` is 2 m = 100 screen pixels (`ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:27`: a metre is 50 pixels), a level unit is H / 256 pixels, so the limit is 100 x 256 / H units: 35.6 at 720, 23.7 at 1080, 17.8 at 1440, 11.9 at 2160. `Tuning::screenPxPerUnit` is the reference 720 / 256 until `MagicPortalsLayer::stepLevel` sets it from the viewport's height over the view's 256; every suite and every route replay publishes 1280 x 720 or none, so a route flies the same on every window. It is route-neutral at 720 (a fall of 590 units).
5. **G10-5c(2) IS NOT BUILT, WITH ITS SCAN.** `out/parity/program/CAP/slope_scan.py` over the 128 levels lists every static top that slopes against the hold's limit with the DECODED floor friction (`sqrt(0.9 x f)`: platform 23.0 degrees, ramps 25.4, bridge01 33.9, block00 31.0): the ramps (16 of them, 14.0 degrees) and bridge01 (46 at 14 degrees, one at 6, one at 20) hold either way; **five levels have a surface the decoded mix would not hold and the 0.949 does: 1-29 (block00 40, 50 degrees), 2-11 (single_block_plat 35, 55), 2-22 (bridge01 34, 0.1 degree over), 3-20 (block00 40, 50) and 3-29 (single_block_plat 30, 60)**; 1-02's 24 block00s at 45 and 4-15's two double_block_plats at 45 are past 43.5 either way. Beyond the limit the player is steered as before, which is the frictionless creep (0.48 units a tick at 30 degrees, 1.111 x sin x cos), unmeasured against the original's slow slide (its idle x is set to 0 every update and its friction acts on what is left); swapping the port's too-sticky hold for a too-slippery creep is not a gain, so the row stays open with both numbers. (1) the corner probes and (3), (4) are unchanged.
6. **EVERY LEVEL START LANDS A LITTLE HARDER, AND THE FIRST QUAKE OF A LEVEL BEGINS WITH A BACK** (deviation 3, from four layer tests that failed on it). The markers put the player where the Godot 44-tall capsule rested; the original's body is 3.9 units shorter and falls 3.9 units further (level30: lands on tick 3, `player_impact` hit 1.333, a 0.28-unit tremble), which is what the original's own physics gives (the library stills put its player 9.2 px, 3.3 units, lower than the port's old one did). `player_impact`'s gate is `hit_above` 0, so any landing shakes, and a tremble below the generator's stop (1 px) is a forth with no back: the generator keeps its `forth` flag, as the original's does (`earthquake.json`, `Generator::Update`), so the NEXT quake begins with the back of that one (-0.28 units, then the sequence halved). The two quake cases now run one quake out before they measure their own (`LetTheLandingPass`).

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on every level.**
- **The player is shorter, narrower and lower**: 18.2 wide and 36.2 tall (20 x 44 before), so he fits a gap 1.8 units narrower and 7.8 units lower than before, his sides meet a wall 0.9 units later (4-01's pillar stops him at x 151.85, 153.0 before), and **he stands 3.9 units lower on whatever he stands on - a floor, a ramp, a crate, a barrel - with the sprite following** (his drawn feet were 9.2 px above the library stills' on flat floors, they are 1.7 px below).
- **Triggers see the real shape**: a death area, a goal and a portal's entry (and every other overlap test that reads his collider) judge the 18.2 x 36.2 capsule (the death-area octagon kills on 1 unit of overlap of the capsule's side 9.1 from his centre, 10 before). A portal's entry moves with it: 2-12's walk now enters its first portal's trigger before the pair exists (the second portal lands on tick 107, not 105; the entry edge is INFERRED from `Portals.cpp`) and walks through it with no teleport.
- **Portal shots leave from, and the head-height retry is measured from, the player's entity point, which is now 3.9 units lower**: `Portals.cpp`'s `fromPx` is the shooter's transform (the capsule's centre, now the original's entity point) and the retry's offset `retry_from_units` (0, -30) in `placement.json` is decoded relative to the original's entity point, so it now stands where the original's does and no capsule-derived constant is left stale. By the verifier's reading this is what turns the first shots of 2-11, 4-07, 2-17 and 3-31 into the "after the head-height retry" failures in the census below: route timing, not a new rule.
- **His ground sensor stands where the original puts it, 18 below the entity**; a minion's body still holds him (unchanged: the spec's reversal was not built, decision 1).
- **A level opens with him falling 3.9 units further** onto the floor (a tick or two later, with a landing tremble of about 0.3 units, decision 6).
- **A fall is held to 100 screen pixels a step on the screen it is played on** (23.7 units on a 1080 window, 35.6 on 720): only a body that falls more than about 253 units at 1080 reaches it.
- Not changed: his weight (0.104, step 152), his friction (the port's 0; the .ent's 0.9 is the hold's), the walk, the air brake, the fall, the hold.

**THE DECISIONS TO SEE FIRST (for the orchestrator and the owner).**

1. **THE SPEC'S "CARRIED BY FRICTION, AS THE ORIGINAL DOES" IS NOT WHAT THE FILES SHOW, AND WAS NOT BUILT AS WRITTEN.** The spec and G10-5c(3) say the original's friction carries a player along a platform that moves sideways under him. `moving_platform` is `static="1"` in all 15 placements; `ETHPhysicsSimulator::CreateBody` makes `IsStatic()` a `b2_staticBody` (`ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:68`, density 0 at `:107`); and `linearMotion`'s `SetPosition` reaches `ETHPhysicsEntityController::SetPosXY` (`ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp:98-103`), which is `b2Body::SetTransform` and `SetAwake(true)` on that body alone. A static body teleported that way **has no velocity**: Box2D's friction acts on the relative tangent velocity (0 for the platform), so nothing is carried by it, and what stands on the body is pushed out along the contact's normal by the position solver as it rises, or falls under gravity as it goes down (the callback has to `awakeEntitiesAround` for the same reason: a static body's `SetTransform` wakes nothing). And **no platform moves sideways**: its call is `linearMotion(thisEntity, vertical = true, angle = 0, startAngle = 0)` (`ETHCallback_moving_platform` ins 1-10); the sideways movers are the horizontal agents, which have no body, and the lifts (`lift.ent`, `static=1` too, `AddToPositionXY`: the same SetTransform), which are G2's and left behind by a player the same way. G10-5c(3) is therefore **not a behaviour of the original** (INFERRED from the decode; no clip shows a rider: the footage index has none) and nothing was built for it; the row closes as a refuted premise. What was built: the port moves the body with the velocity that gets it there (`Mover::MoveKinematic`), which the engine's solver reads, so a rider is carried UP and DOWN by that velocity, his feet within 0.01 unit of the top both ways (the platform's friction is `friction 1` held, WT-4, and the player's is 0), the first call being a bare teleport. **That is the port's carry, not the original's**: the original pushes a rider out of a rising platform by the position solver (a lag behind the top) and leaves him to fall under gravity as it goes down (INFERRED from the decode; the second verifier's arithmetic, `verify1.json` problem 1, not measured: gravity adds 0.556 unit a tick of speed each tick against 1-11's block descending at 1.17 units a tick at its fastest, so he is airborne for a few ticks of each landing). No clip shows a rider; deviations 1 and 4 are the record, and the throwaway build that would show whether the engine's push-out holds him is deviation 4's **Next**.
2. **THE SWING IS linearMotion'S, NOT HALF THE AMPLITUDE AT TWICE THE RATE.** `position = the node's point + cos(angle) x stride`, the angle stepped by `speed x the script's milliseconds / 1000` BEFORE the cosine is read, from a start angle of 0: **the node's point is the middle of the swing and `stride` its amplitude, `speed` its rate in radians a second, and the first call writes the position already a stride along its axis** (down the screen), where the Godot project had `sin(2 x speed x t) x stride / 2` from the placed point. `Mover::Oscillation` is `Motion::Linear` over the node's own `speed` and `stride` (the one arithmetic the crystals, the keys, the portals' hover and the ghost already read, `Motion::Advance`, with the cosine from `DetMath` by `Motion::OffsetPxWithCosine`, the contract the swing has always kept), on the script's whole 16 ms a tick. **Checked on the original's own library stills** (`G3/library_fit.md`): 1-11's block stands at y 208.7, 124.1 and 230.0 (60 units above its placed point in the second frame; the old swing's limit is 35) and the horizontal agent of the same level at x 355.3, 398.0 and 376.6: one phase, 0.88 s, fits BOTH to **1.75 units rms (4.9 px), worst 2.4**, where the old half swing leaves 30.8; 1-06, 2-26 and 3-28 are seen at 63.6 of 64, 38.4 of 48 and 66.1 of 72 and fit to 1.34, 0.70 and 1.64 u (old: 27.9, 20.3, 39.3).
3. **THE FIRST CALL IS A TELEPORT WITH NO VELOCITY.** It jumps the body a stride from where the level placed it (1-11's block 70 units, 4-22's 110); written as the velocity that gets it there it would throw whatever touches the new place a stride in one step. `Mover::PlaceKinematic` sets the transform and a velocity of 0 on that tick, as the original's SetTransform does; every later tick is `MoveKinematic` (pinned: velocity x 1/60 equals the tick's displacement to 1e-3).
4. **AN AGENT IS TESTED BEFORE IT MOVES.** `ETHCallback_anti_portal_agent` runs its shot-in-flight arm (ins 1-199) first and `linearMotion` last (ins 200-250), so a shot meets the agent where its LAST frame wrote it, and the frame's move is what is drawn and what the next frame's shot meets. `Portals::State::Tick` advanced `motion.t` first and tested the agent a tick ahead - up to 2.3 units on 1-11's fast agent, more than the 0.6 px the route notes cite. It now advances every agent after the shots it flew; the callback pass reads where the agent stands, and the spawn pass of a tap's own frame (whose static callback ran before that advance) reads `Agent::BeforeLastMovePx`, where it stood before it. The pinned case: a shot fired 22.0 behind the point the agent has just left, the agent moving away (24 from where it is now), kills it on the spawn pass.
5. **THE ZONE PATROL BRANCH IS GONE.** `Portals.cpp` swung a no-portal zone with a speed and a stride on the Godot project's axis; no `antiportal` callback calls `linearMotion` (`ETHCallback_antiportal`, bytes 335020..335206) and no placed ring has a speed since step 126 made the agents agents. `NoPortalZone` lost `moving` and `motion`; a ring stands where the level places it.
6. **THE BUCKET CLOCK IS NOT MODELLED, AND FOUR MOVERS ARE AFFECTED** (deviation 2). A static entity's callback runs only from the visible-bucket loop (`ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:70-88`, `ETHScene.cpp:541-574`), buckets of 128 units intersecting the screen PLUS ONE RING (`ETHScene.cpp:54`, `:69`: `drawingBorderBuckets` true; `ETHBucketManager.cpp:52-90`). **The original's camera opens on `camera_start`, near the exit, and eases to the player from its first frame** (the layer's note at `MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:657-665`; the port opens on the player, the owner's choice), so a mover near the exit runs during the pan and stops after it, and one the camera never comes near has not made its first call. With the camera on the player at the spawn, **four of the 18 movers stand outside the drawn buckets**: 3-03's and 3-06's `moving_platform_1011` (x 672), 1-11's `anti_portal_agent_639` (x 674) and 3-09's `moving_platform_1429` (x 96, the spawn at x 617) (computed from the level files, the level's `max` node as the right limit). How long each runs during the pan is not known (the camera's ease is not decoded here). The port's convention for every static callback is to run from the level's first tick (a crystal's bob, the ghost, the lifts: the project-wide row), and the spec's own sweep gate ("each explained by the phase at tick 420") assumes it.
7. **THE BODY MOVES BEFORE THE STEP, A FRAME AHEAD OF THE ORIGINAL'S CONTACT** (deviation 3), as every mover here does (a door, a bobbing slab, a lift): the original's callbacks run after its physics step (`ETHScene::Update`, `ETHScene.cpp:464-490`), so what a step meets is the position the frame before wrote; the port's step meets this tick's. At most one tick's travel (1.15 units on the fastest platform); the picture drawn after the tick is the original's.
8. **CAP-7 IS CLOSED BY THIS RELINK.** The sources of step 153's comment-only edits (`Player.cpp`, `test_mp_player.cpp`, `Portals.hpp`, `Puzzle.hpp`, `keys.json`, `gravitywell.json`) are in the executables that measured every gate here: `test_mp.exe` `a72d460d` (one launch with no argument; the first, alone, on `test_mp_movers`) and `MagicPortals.exe` `aa85e2b9`.

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on 12 levels** (the 11 with a moving platform: 1-06, 1-11, 2-26, 2-28, 2-31, 3-03, 3-06, 3-09, 3-28, 4-12, 4-22; and 3-14's agent; 1-11 has both).
- **Every moving platform swings twice as far, at half the rate, from a stride along its axis.** The 15 platforms swing `stride` either side of their placed point (1-11's block y 114 to 254, was 149 to 219; 1-06's y 80 to 208; 4-12's `moving_platform_2251` y 0 to 192; 2-26's `_960` 88 to 228), at `speed` radians a second (the period doubles: 1-11's 6.28 s, was 3.14), and they **start a stride DOWN the screen from where the level places them**, not at the placed point (the first tick puts 1-11's block at y 254, its top at 238: 14 units under the island floor, y 224, it was placed beside). Their peak speed is unchanged (stride x speed, 70 units a second on 1-11's), their turnarounds half as hard. A platform now reaches places it did not and rests where it did not.
- **The three patrolling anti-portal agents swing twice as far at half the rate** (1-11's `_639` 60 +- 48 vertically at 3 rad/s, `_599` 384 +- 36 horizontally at 2; 3-14's `anti_portal_agent_1334` 64 +- 32 at 2), so a shot's kill window against them moves (3-14's route, which killed it on tick 129, no longer does), and **a shot meets an agent where its last frame put it**.
- **A rider is carried as before, by velocity both ways** (the port's carry, not the original's push-out up and fall down: decision 1; a player on 1-11's block keeps his feet within 0.01 unit of its top through a whole swing, no drift in x); **the platform's gate** (nothing goes through a placed pair while a platform is at a portal) reads the same bodies, in their new places (level5's: held 201 ticks, through on tick 370).
- Not changed: a lift, a door, a ring, a shock agent (`Fields` already swung its ring as `cos(angle) x stride`), the player.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing, `ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp`, `ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp`, `ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp`, `ETHScene.cpp`, the library stills and `WT`'s and `CAP`'s world are all there. The spec's premise about friction was decided by the decode (decision 1), not blocked on.

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS** (each an open row in `docs/parity-backlog.md`, G3-1 to G3-8).
1. **The spec's carry premise is refuted, not built** (decision 1): no friction carry in the original, a vertical riding only; G10-5c(3) closes. INFERRED from the decode: no clip of a rider exists, so the original's rider (a push-out lag of about 1.5 units into a rising platform at the fastest, by Box2D's position solver: INFERRED, not measured) is not compared with the port's (0.01).
2. **The bucket clock is not modelled** (decision 6): four movers (3-03's and 3-06's `moving_platform_1011`, 1-11's `anti_portal_agent_639`, 3-09's `moving_platform_1429`) start on tick 1 and never pause where the original's run only while the camera is near them, in the opening pan and again if the camera returns; every other static callback is in the same row. The camera positions are computed (the spawn's x less half the view, clamped by the level's `max` node), not captured. **The route phase should know it** for those levels: the routes of 3-03, 3-06, 3-09 and 1-11 will be authored on the port's convention (every static callback from tick 1), not on the original's phase, and are marked so, so that the owner does not take their timing as the original's (`verify1.json` problem 2; building the bucket clock is the other way out: LEFT FOR LATER).
3. **A platform moves before its step, a frame ahead of the original's contact** (decision 7): at most 1.15 units; the picture is the original's.
4. **The port carries by velocity, the original by push-out**: a body pressed against a platform's SIDE would be dragged by the port's contact friction where the original's (a static body, no velocity) is not - the player's friction is 0 so he is not, a crate's (friction 1, held: WT-4) would be; not measured on any body but the player's. **Next:** a throwaway build that places a platform's body with no velocity every tick (`PlaceKinematic`), measured with the player standing on 1-11's block (`verify1.json` problem 1): if the engine's push-out holds him, the original's behaviour is adopted; otherwise an engine gap is recorded with the number. A source edit and one relink, so not part of this step.
5. **The phase is confirmed only to about 0.2 s, and only on 1-11** (`library_fit.md`; the second verifier's t-series fit, `verify1.json` problem 3, added there): the rate and the amplitude are confirmed; the start of the clock is the HUD's in an h-series still, and the h phases 0.75 to 1.57 s differ by level (1-06's 1.57 s unexplained). The verifier's independent fit of 1-11's t2.0, t4.5 and t8.0 stills (block centres 163.2, 157.2 and 187.9 units, measured by it, not by this step) gives the full swing at 2.13 u rms with a phase of -0.17 s, about the port's level-start phase (the old swing 18.2 u rms), which supports tick 1 as a stride along with a clock running from the level's start, on that level only.
6. **`awakeEntitiesAround` is not built**: the engine wakes what rests on a kinematic body itself (`engine/src/core/PhysicsSystem.cpp:1089-1095`).

## Step 156 - the portal tap as the original handles it: the tap-time ray decides where the shot goes and whether it fails, only a tap that reaches the hourglass restarts the 400 ms, a blocker reads the shot's position, and the zero-g recoil aims at finalPos (built)

**THE PROGRAM'S R23** (`docs/parity-backlog.md` section 6, the rulings "decided for what the original does, and not built", the rows G4-1, G4-2 and G4-8 and the "Order 10.1" rows; decode D3 with its check; program wave 3b-2, the first of its four steps - R23, G9, G1a, G1b - run on MPR `main` after step 155, engine `710bffc` unmoved, nothing else running during the timing steps; committed locally, **not pushed**: `origin/main` is `00de2b1`). Before: HEAD `00de2b1`, `MagicPortals.exe` `098e51b4`, `test_mp.exe` `e32d8d0b` (step 155's verifier: 53 suites, 28,723 checks, 86 of 86 routes won), the standing sweep `out/parity/program/R3b/fix1/after/sweep/`. Changed: `game/sim/Portals.{hpp,cpp}` (`Shoot` runs `Predict` and the shot flies by its answer; the order of the tap's tests; `Insert`; `flyOnePass`; `Flight::said`, `Tap::said`), `game/sim/Shot.{hpp,cpp}` (`InsideBox`; `FirstBodyPassing` gone: the shot meets no body), `game/sim/Game.cpp` and `GravityWell.hpp` (`shotPasses` gone), `game/MagicPortalsLayer.{cpp,hpp}` (the fire-diamond byte handed to `Shoot`; `queueTapEffects` reads the stored answer), `game/data/placement.json` (`final_pos.fire_diamond_reach` 64 and the notes), `game/data/gravitywell.json` and `effects.json` (notes), `data/entity_roles.json` (`no_portal` leaves `no_portal_zone` for `scenery_hint`), and the suites `tests/test_mp_shot.cpp` (266 to 1,351 checks), `test_mp_layer.cpp`, `test_mp_movers.cpp`, `test_mp_wells.cpp`, `docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 20 and `docs/parity-backlog.md`. No engine change (the pin stays `710bffc`), no converter change, **no route file touched**. The evidence is under `out/parity/program/R23/` (`impl.md`; `census.md`; `captures/`).

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on every tap.**
- **Where a shot goes is where the tap-time ray ends, not the tap.** A shot flew to the tap and failed on the first solid body it met; it now flies to `computePortalFinalPos`'s `finalPos` - the contact for a wall or a body a portal may not open on, **10 units past the contact (inside it) for a teleportable one** - and does there what the ray said: a doomed shot (red_cross at the tap) opens `portal_fail` at the contact, any other opens its portal. So **a crate, a stone or a minion now takes the portal** (116 placed bodies in 62 levels and 60 minion spawns in 35, which the ray let through and the flight stopped on), **a button, a `destroyier.ent` and the anchor doom the shot at their face** (46 buttons in 37 levels, 4 destroyiers, 1 anchor: sensors the ray stops on and the flight passed), **the head-height retry is the shot's own** (a low box a tap clears from over the head no longer stops the shot; a retry that meets a beam dooms a shot the flight would have landed), and **a reflected leg lands 10 units short of a wall instead of dying on it**.
- **The shot meets nothing on its way.** A platform, a crate or a door that comes into the line after the tap stops nothing (`projectile.ent` has no shape); a gravity well's agent was already passed (step 125) and the ray passes it by name. An `anti_projectile_wall` kills a shot whose POSITION its rectangle holds on a frame (up to one advance, 3.2 units, later than the swept box did); a shot that arrives is gone before it looks.
- **A portal can open inside a no-portal field** when the ray's end is 10 units inside a body whose contact lay outside the field: `insertPortal` tests no field (the port refused it). A doomed shot's red end is `portal_fail_in_antiportal` and a shake of 5 when the shot's position - up to 3.2 units past the destiny - is in a field (the port asked the destiny).
- **The 400 ms**: a tap that gets as far as the hourglass restarts it, so a second tap within 400 ms of an hourglass tap is silent (the port left the clock running). The cooldown refusal and the budget-0 tap restart nothing (the program's spec said every refusal; the listing says these two do not, and the listing is what is built). Budget 0 keeps its red_waves (B) and shake of 7 (built in step 103, pinned again).
- **The zero-gravity recoil is away from `finalPos`**, not from the tap (after a wall's contact or a retry's end the direction can differ by a few degrees).
- **`no_portal_705` (1-07) is no zone** (the sign's picture; `AntiPortalManager` gathers only `antiportal` and `antiportal.ent`; it lay inside `antiportal_687`'s field, so no tap's answer moves).
Nothing else moves: the flight (step 149), R1's radius, R2's wells, R17's agents, G8's flames, G6's fireballs, the torch's kill, the marks' pictures and positions.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing has every function the decode needs (`PortalManager::update`, `managePortalInsertion`, `blockPortalEffects`, `computePortalFinalPos` (method and global), `addProjectile`, `insertPortal`, `ETHCallback_projectile`, `ETHCallback_anti_projectile_wall`, `isPointInRect`, `isTeleportable`, `applyImpulse`; md5 `48fe65ce` verified), and the port already had the ray (`Portals::State::Predict`, step 103) and the sampled static callbacks (step 149). The spec's "(1) a refused tap (budget 0, flight, cooldown) restarts the clock" is broader than the decode (see GAMEPLAY): built as decoded, and said here.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 20 has the citations): `update` returns inside the level's first 300 ms and hands budget 0 to `blockPortalEffects`; `managePortalInsertion` per touch refuses silently inside 400 ms or on a pad or button (#43-73), then **resets `lastPortalTimer` (#75-78)**, then shows the hourglass if `SeekEntity('projectile.ent')` finds one (#181-210) or fires: `computePortalFinalPos`, `vibrate 30` on `hasFailed`, `applyImpulse(finalPos)`, `addProjectile(finalPos, hasFailed, absTouchPos)`. The projectile flies to `destiny = finalPos` and, once its position has gone past it, calls `insertPortal` (no field, no budget test of its own: it kills the oldest above `maxPortals`) or, if `willDie`, draws `portal_fail` at the destiny - `portal_fail_in_antiportal` with a shake of 5 when its POSITION is in a field - and plays the failed sound.

**WHAT IS BUILT.** `State::Shoot` takes the tap in the original's order - no shooter, `update`'s first gate, budget 0, the 400 ms (silent, no clock), **the clock restarts**, a shot flying (the hourglass) - and then calls `Predict` (or the fire-diamond branch, `final_pos.fire_diamond_reach` x the aim, with the leftover byte the layer hands in), stores the answer on the `Flight` (`said`: destiny, `willDie`, what the ray met) and on the `Tap`, and aims the recoil at it. `Tick`'s `flyOnePass` no longer sweeps bodies; a blocker is `Shot::InsideBox` of the position the pass left; an arrival is `Insert` at the destiny, or the failure the ray said, with `Failure.inField` read at `positionPx` (the position after the advance, past the destiny); a reflector's turn still comes from the swept reach (G9) but the new leg takes `FinalPosFrom(..., hasBeenReflected)`'s end and verdict. The layer's `queueTapEffects` reads the stored answer (no second `Predict`), so the mark and the shot's end are one answer.

## Step 157 - the reflector as the original has it: a shot caught by a position sample within 32 units, mirrored on the plane's axis (or on the side it came from, where the placement has no plane), and sent on from the reflector's own point for the length it was fired or the way it came, by one reflector at most (built)

**THE PROGRAM'S G9** (`docs/parity-backlog.md` section 6, the major "G9. The reflector catches within `size.x` (32) and its leg is `min(|caster - agent|, remaining)`", the rows G4-2's third part, G4-4 and R23-1; program wave 3b-2, the second of its four steps - R23, G9, G1a, G1b - run on MPR `main` after step 156 (`8e81ccf`), engine `710bffc` unmoved; built and measured here, independently verified (below), and committed locally as the step's own commit, **not pushed**: `origin/main` is `00de2b1`). **THE TOOLCHAIN MOVED UNDER THE STEP, and the first thing done was to prove it moved nothing.** The Build Tools' MSVC went from 14.50.35717 to 14.51.36231 on 2026-10-05 and the old toolset is gone, so `build/` (which cached the old compiler's path) could not build at all ("CreateProcess failed"). `build/` was deleted and `tools/parity/port_build.bat` configured it afresh (Ninja, Release, validation on, `cl`, the SDK's glslc) and built `MagicPortals` on the CLEAN tree before any edit: 0 `warning C` (only the 12 vendored-file D9025 notes), `MagicPortals.exe` `eb8ced80`; 1-01, 1-12 and 2-25 at f420 on it are **byte-identical** to `R23/after/sweep/` (md5 `6141ca6b`, `1a9f5116` and `bc3e5ada`), so the new compiler changed no picture and R23's sweep is this step's "before". (`CLAUDE.md`'s environment line still says toolset 14.50; it is the owner's file and was left.)

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on the 19 levels with a reflector** (23 placements: 1-12 (3), 1-13, 1-20, 1-21 (2), 1-23, 1-29, 2-10, 2-11, 2-16, 2-18, 2-25, 2-27, 3-03, 3-05, 3-14 (2), 3-25, 3-26, 4-10 and 4-23; 9 horizontal, 13 vertical, one with no plane; none carries a scale).
- **A reflector catches a shot within 32 units, not 16, and by a sample, not along the way.** The shot is caught when the position it has once a frame (at its spawn on the tap's frame, 27.2 units out on its first callback, then every 3.2) is STRICTLY within 32 x the placement's scale of the reflector's point; a shot passing 16 to 32 units from one is now turned (it flew through before), a shot fired from within 32 of one is turned at once, and a shot that arrives inside the circle with no earlier sample inside is not caught (it deletes itself before the reflector looks). Pinned: 31 off is caught, 33 off is not, exactly 32.0 off is not.
- **The turned shot leaves the REFLECTOR, and flies as far as it was fired or as far as it came.** The port sent the shot on from where it was caught for the rest of its way; the listing's new shot is spawned at the reflector's point, jumps 24 from there on its first callback, and flies `min(sqrt(squaredDistance), distance(casterPos, reflector))` - the whole length the old shot was fired (never decremented), or the way from where its leg began to the reflector, whichever is less (the program's spec said "remaining": the listing is what is built). 1-12's reflect_agent_761 from the player's point (73, 204) with a tap at 1.5 times the way to it: the old rule opened the portal at (200.1, 168.4), 39 units on from the catch point (worked out by hand from the old code: entry to the 16-circle, the rest of the way to the first leg's end, y flipped); it opens at (287, 204), 124.7 from the reflector. A head-on shot fired 300 units at a vertical reflector 100 from the shooter: it opened at (-32, 200) (184 less the 216 left); it opens at (100, 200), the way it came. So the leg is much longer where the tap was at or short of the reflector (1-12's: 39 to 124.7) and shorter where it was far beyond it (the head-on case: 216 to 100), and a longer leg keeps the shot in the air, so a second tap meets the hourglass for longer (four of the six new route failures).
- **A shot comes off one reflector at most**, as the port's `max_reflections` already said, now the decoded rule (the shot a reflector adds has `reflect` 0 and every reflector returns on such a shot; `addProjectile` has two callers in the whole listing, the tap's with 1 and this callback's with 0): the reflected leg flies through every other reflector. Pinned with two reflectors in a row.
- **A reflector with no plane mirrors by the side the shot is on.** `computeReflectVector`'s `''` arm snaps `normalize(shot - reflector)` to the nearest of four axes (`getRightAngleVector`): a shot from the left or right flips x, one from above or below flips y. The port read it as vertical. The one such placement is 2-27's `reflect_agent_ent_961` (the handle's reflector, step 139).
Nothing else moves: the flight (step 149), the tap's ray and the 10-short landing of a reflected shot (step 156), the marks, the flash and the sound (already the callback's: `projectile_shoot` where the old shot was, the mark at the clipped new end, `red_waves` (A) where the new ray meets nothing in a field, `playReflectSound`), the handle's follow.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing has every function the decode needs (`ETHCallback_reflect_agent`, `computeReflectVector`, `getRightAngleVector`, `reflect`, `squaredDistance`, `seekNeighbourEntity`, `ProjectileChooser::choose`, `addProjectile`, `ETHCallback_projectile`; md5 `48fe65ce` verified); `getAngle`, `GetSize` and `GetString` are the engine's (`ETHScriptObjRegister.cpp:103-107`, `ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-682`, `ETHEntity.cpp:872-877`), read. The sprite is 32 x 32 (`reflect_agent.png` read from the file, `reflect_agent.ent`: SpriteCut 1 x 1, Scale 1.0, empty custom data). Two readings of the spec were corrected from the listing, and are said here because they are gameplay: (1) the leg is `min(|caster - agent|, sqrt(squaredDistance))`, the whole fired length, **not** "remaining" (#158-180: the stored `squaredDistance` is `addProjectile`'s #94-110 and `ETHCallback_projectile` only reads it, no `SetFloat` anywhere in it); (2) "chaining through several reflectors" does not exist in the original: `reflect` is 0 on the shot a reflector adds (#224-227) and every reflector returns on such a shot (#39-54). `addProjectile`'s seventh argument (0 from the tap, 1 from this callback) is read by nothing in its body, so it moves no mark and no sound.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 21 has every citation; `shot.json` `reflection._note` the same in the data): a static callback (`reflect_agent.ent` is `static="1" shape="0"`), after the frame's dynamic ones. #1-6 `doFollow`; #8-27 the first `projectile.ent` in its bucket and the eight round it; #39-54 its `reflect` must be set; #55-84 `squaredDistance(projectile, agent) < size.x x size.x`, `size` = `GetSize()` = the sprite's frame x the entity's scale = 32; #92-146 `normal = computeReflectVector(normalize(projectilePos - agentPos), GetString('plane'))`, `newDir = reflect(direction, normal)`; #148-196 `dist = min(sqrt(squaredDistance), distance(casterPos, agentPos))`, `newDest = agentPos + newDir x dist`; #198-221 `computePortalFinalPos(newDest, ..., casterPos = agentPos, ..., hasBeenReflected)` clips it; #224-235 `addProjectile(newDest, hasFailed, newDest, agentPos, pref, 0, 1)` adds the shot AT the agent (`addProjectile` #26-40: `vector3(casterPos, 0)`); #237-243 deletes the old one; #245-260 `projectile_shoot.ent` at the old one's position; #264-266 `playReflectSound`.

**WHAT IS BUILT.** `flyOnePass`'s reflector arm is a sample like the blocker's, the agent's and the flame's: `Reaches(next, reflector.centrePx, shot.reflectSizeUnits x reflector.scale)` (strict, centre to centre, `next` being the pass's one position sample), skipped when the shot arrives, run on the spawn pass too, and while `flight->reflections < shot.maxReflections`. The turn block is #92-243: `dir` = the leg's stored direction (`toPx - fromPx`, normalised), `normal = Shot::ReflectNormal(plane, normalize(caught - agent))`, `newDir = Shot::Reflect(dir, normal)`, `length = min(|toPx - fromPx|, |fromPx - agent|)`, `newDest = agent + newDir x length`, `FinalPosFrom(newDest, agent, true)` for the clip and the verdict, and the flight is set to start AT the agent (`atPx` and `fromPx`, so the next callback's jump is 24 from there, and a leg's casterPos is where it was added). `Reflection` records the catch sample (the old shot's flash), the unclipped `newDest` (red_waves (A)) and the agent's point (the new leg's start); `MagicPortalsLayer` needed no change (its queue is already the callback's order: waves, mark, flash). A placement's `plane` is `Shot::Plane` (none: `Snap`) and its `scale` is read like an anti-portal agent's.

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on the 35 levels that place a knight** (3-01 to 3-12, 3-15 to 3-24, 3-26, 3-27, 3-29 to 3-32 and 4-25 to 4-31: the program's 34 levels with a patrolling knight, and 3-32's black one; `survey.json`).
- **A knight looks, every frame, and a sighting stands it still.** It sees the player (and a placed portal) when the target's own 128-unit bucket is one of three in ITS row - its own and the next two along the way it faces, so within about 256 to 384 units ahead and the same `floor(y / 128)` - inside a cone of 60 degrees each side of its facing, with a ray from it to the target that meets nothing but another knight or the player. It does not turn, chase or run: on the first frame of a sighting its dwell clock (`elapsedTime`) is zeroed, and again every time its shot gate opens, so a knight whose waypoint holds it 2000 ms or more **does not walk on while it sees the player**; one still on its first leg (holdTime 0) walks on regardless. The frame of the sighting itself still walks (its dwell was read before the reset). A knight that holds with something in sight is not given its standing frame: it keeps its stride's.
- **The exclamation and its sound.** A NEW sighting (targetSpotted 0 to 1) shows `exclamation.ent` 36 units above the knight and plays `enemy_spotted` once the knight's own clock, which starts at 3500 ms, has passed 4000: a sighting that goes on shows nothing, and the first one a level can show is at 500 ms.
- **A blocked way is searched, not walked.** Each frame a ray runs from the knight to the waypoint it walks to (every body but the knights', `char_feet.ent`, `crate_small`, `shock_agent` and `shock_agent.ent` blocks it, by those names as spelled: a placed `crate_small.ent` blocks), and the knight walks only down a clear way. A knight lifted off its floor by a portal, dropped or thrown where that ray is blocked **stands and looks right two seconds and left two** (elapsedTime mod 4000), showing `question.ent` every 4000 ms of its own clock (from 3000), with `minion_question` if the mark is on screen and the way had been clear since the last. The port's old patrol walked on toward the waypoint's x. All 174 patrol legs of the 35 levels are clear in the static level (`test_mp_sight`), so no patrol that played freezes.
- **The dark levels** (4-25, 4-26, 4-27, 4-29, 4-30, 4-31): the knights are blind exactly while the ambient is the darkest value (the level's start, and after a torch is put out). Blind, they still see a **portal** and do not see the **player**, and their way is blocked by the player's body (the two circles of `dark_mage.ent`). A lit torch (ambient `(0.1, 0.1, 0.25)`) gives the sight back. The task's wording "see only while a torch is lit" is the player alone.
- **`anti_sight_wall.ent` has its purpose**: a sensor body that blocks the look's ray and the way's (17 placements in 16 of the converted levels; 16 in the 15 of the 35 knight levels that have one, 3-32's two among them).
- **What does NOT change**: the knights shoot nothing and kill nothing (G1b; their shot GATE runs and records a `ShotDue`, because a shot resets the dwell clock and so decides when a knight walks), the seven stealth achievements still unlock whenever the knights all stand (`SpottedCount()` is still 0 - G1b wires `Minions::State::SpotCount()`), the 2-32 knight (`dragon_knight`) never sees, the sounds `enemy_shot*` are G1b's.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing has every function the decode needs (`ETHCallback_minion`, `findEntityInSight`, `addEnemyShoot`, `ETHCallback_enemy_shoot`, `isPointInScreen`, `dp2`, `equalsAny`, `splitString`, `GameStateController::isFinished`/`finishGame`, `spottedCount`, `hasBeenUnnoticed`; md5 `48fe65ce` verified), and the engine's side (`ETHBucketManager`, `ETHRayCastCallback`, `ETHEntityChooser`, `ETHPhysicsSimulator::GetClosestContact`) is read. Four readings of the spec or the repository's notes were corrected from the listing, each said here because it is gameplay: (1) **there IS a sight range**: the three buckets (`minions.json`'s old note said "no radius ... the bucket walk is not a range" and put the bucket at 256: it is 128, `Game::start` #3-17 and `docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 4); (2) **there is no chase and no turn**: `moveVec` is written only by the walk and search arms; (3) **`cantReach` is write-only**: its one occurrence in the listing is the `0` the walk writes (#997-1009), nothing reads it - the probe's result is the local `isInSight`, and what the original does with a blocked way is the search arm; (4) **a blind knight still sees a portal**, and the player blocks its way. Also found, not changed: `placement.json anti_portal_agent.bucket_units` (256, with a note that `Game::start` pushes no bucket size) contradicts `Game::start` #3-17 and #49 (R17 recorded that it moves no answer).

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 22 has every citation; `decode.md` the whole machine; `minions.json` `sight` the numbers). `findEntityInSight` (#56-267): the entities STORED in the agent's bucket, the next and the one after along `moveVec` (`GetBucket` is `floor(p / 128)`); for each, in that order, a name test (`portal.ent`, and `dark_mage.ent` while `canSeeAnything`), `dp2(moveVec, normalize(target - agent)) > 0.5` (strict), and `GetClosestContact(agent, target, ..., 'ghost_minion.ent;minion.ent;dark_mage.ent') == null`; Box2D's ray cast reports sensors, so every body but the named ones blocks. `ETHCallback_minion` #578-898: the sighting block above; #899-996 the way's ray and `isInSight`; #977-1163 the walk (clear way and `elapsedTime > holdTime`); #1164-1228 the hold arm (brake, the standing frame only with nothing in sight); #1229-1449 the search arm. `canSeeAnything` is `!(DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT == GetAmbientLight())`, which `Lighting::Ambient` already computes for the drawing. `dragon_knight` calls neither function; `anti_sight_wall.ent` and the two marks have no callback.

**WHAT IS BUILT.** `Minions::State::Tick(registry, step, senses)` is the callback in its own order: the three clocks, the arrival (unchanged), `Look` (the facing is the one the last walk or search left, so a knight that has never walked sees nothing for its first tick), the sighting block with the shot's gate (`ShotDue` recorded, `elapsedMs` and `shootMs` zeroed as #843-868 zero them; nothing is spawned), the way's ray (`RayClear`: `Shot::ClosestContact` over the registry's bodies, triggers included, with the knights' bodies and the bodies the level places under the listed names ignored - `BindSight`, by `Roles::EntityName` as spelled - plus, for a blind knight only, the player's two circles by Box2D's own circle ray test), then the walk or the hold (the arm `Watch` when something is in sight, `Search` when the way is blocked and nothing is). Everything numeric is `minions.json` `sight`. `Game::SensesOf` gathers what the engine would tell the callback: the ambient (`Lighting::FileAmbient` of the scene plus the torches and the red key, through `Lighting::Ambient`), `finished` (`goals.completed || hazards.playerDied`), the player's capsule centre and circles, the placed portals. The layer queues the marks from `Minions::State::marks` as effects (`Effects::ExclamationMark`/`QuestionMark`: the knight's entity point less (0, 36), its depth less 32), latches the sounds (the question's only when the point is on screen) and maps the two new arms to the picture (`Watch` sets no frame, `Search` is the arm `art.json minion.search` was written for).

## Step 159 - the knights shoot: an enemy_shoot.ent that kills the player or a portal by its stored id, the contact's hold cap, a stone's crush and a barrel's blast, and the stealth achievements that wait on all of it (built)

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on every level with a knight (35), on the seven with a rolling stone and on 3-19's bombs.**
- **A knight shoots, and the shot kills.** When its gate opens (a sighting 650 ms old - 1000 ms where the target is within 42 units, 3650 where the knight itself moves - and 2000 ms since its last shot: step 158's gate) it fires an `enemy_shoot.ent` at where the sighted entity stood: 16 units out to begin with, flying 120 units a second of the script's clock, with NO body (it passes every wall, door and crate), until it has gone farther than that point is. It is judged against the entity it was aimed at ALONE, by id: within 16 units of it, **a player is killed** (hp 0, the death a death area makes: blood, the lost screen) and **a placed portal is killed** (it leaves the pair, fades 400 ms and is gone; the golden score still counts it); the shot passes the player standing in the line of a shot at a portal, and a portal in the line of a shot at the player. A shot whose target has gone flies on to its destiny. Every shot ENDS in a burst (`portal_fail_in_antiportal.ent`), `startEarthquake(10)` (a visible shake of the whole view, on or off screen) and `enemy_shot_ended`; each leaves with `enemy_shot`, a `portal_mark.ent` ring where it is going and a flash at the muzzle. **The player standing in a knight's row now dies in about 1.6 s of a shot's flight**; a route that walks through a knight's sight is shot (the census below: six of 86 routes die).
- **The player's body caps a knight's hold.** The first step a knight and the player touch, its own hold is `min(hold, 1000)`: a knight serving 5 or 10 s of dwell walks on after at most 1 s once the player has touched it (minion.ent only; the black knight has no such callback).
- **A barrel's blast kills a knight.** `explode` destroys and burns whatever its grabber (80 units, a clear ray) takes: a knight in reach dies the tick after (the flame's one-tick-later burn, `fire32` and blood). 3-19's five bombs stand near its knight; 3-32's barrels near the escorts.
- **A rolling stone crushes a knight it hits.** A stone that begins to touch one at hitIntensity above 1.23 destroys it with a smash sound and a shake of 25. Seven knight levels carry stones (3-07, 3-10, 3-12, 3-15, 3-18, 3-20, 3-22); in the routes it happens on 3-10 (tick 452: the key-carrying knight) and 3-12 (206 and 329).
- **The seven stealth achievements are real.** `SpottedCount()` is `Minions::State::SpotCount()`: 24, 26, 28, 32, 42, 66 and 76 unlock only with exactly their knights standing and none ever having seen (a knight that saw and then died is out of the sum, as `GetEntityArray` no longer holds it). 3-02's route, which unlocked 24 on 401, no longer does.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing has every function (`addEnemyShoot`, `ETHCallback_enemy_shoot`, `killPortal`, `ETHCallback_portal`, `PortalManager::update`/`insertPortal`, `ETHBeginContactCallback_minion`, `..._rolling_stone`, `explode`, `seekNeighbourEntity`, `ByIDChooser`, `isCharacter`, `STimeManager::unitsPerSecond`; md5 `48fe65ce` verified). One correction to step 158's own decode: `addEnemyShoot(finalPos, casterPos, target)` is the listing's signature (the arguments are pushed last-first), so the call is `addEnemyShoot(targetPos, knightPos, target)`; G1a's text had the first two reversed, its `ShotDue` had them right.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 23 has every citation; `decode.md` the whole machine).
- `addEnemyShoot` (#0-176): `dirVector = normalize(finalPos - casterPos)`; `enemy_shoot.ent` at `vector3(casterPos, scale(10))` carrying `direction`, `destiny`, `casterPos`, `targetName` and `targetID`; `portal_mark.ent` at `vector3(finalPos, scale(32))`; `playEnemyShootSound`. No refusal, no cap on live shots.
- `ETHCallback_enemy_shoot`: the first call stores `initialPos`, nudges 16 units, adds `projectile_shoot.ent` and stores `squaredDistance(initialPos, destiny)`; every call frames, turns, moves `dir x scaledUnitsPerSecond(120)`, destroys itself once `squaredDistance(initialPos, position) >` that (strict), looks the target up by `targetID` in its bucket and the eight beside (`seekNeighbourEntity`), and within `scale(16)` of it (strict) sets an `isCharacter`'s `hp` to 0 or `killPortal`s a `portal.ent`, destroying itself either way; a destroyed shot ends in `startEarthquake(10, 0)`, `portal_fail_in_antiportal.ent`, `playEnemyShootExplodeSound`, `DeleteEntity`.
- `killPortal` is two `KillParticleSystem` calls and nothing else; the portal's callback fades it by 0.9 a frame and 400 ms after its systems die adds `portal_death.ent` and deletes it, and `PortalManager::update` pops it at once.
- `ETHBeginContactCallback_minion` #12-55: a non-sensor `dark_mage.ent`'s begin sets the knight's `holdTime = min(holdTime, 1000)`.
- `explode` #111-152 and `ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone` #131-168 are the two deaths (table in `decode.md`); nothing else the knights or the player do kills a knight. There is no sword.

**WHAT IS BUILT.** `Minions::State::Tick` makes the shot where it already recorded the `ShotDue` (the hook G1a left: one record per gate opening, kept for the tests and the layer, and the shot made of it); `State::FlyShots(step, senses)`, called by `Game::AfterStep` after the step and BEFORE the portals' tick, flies each one a tick after it is made, ends it by its range or its stored target, reports the player's death (`playerKilled`, folded into `Hazards` as the other seven are) and the placed portals to kill (`Portals::State::KillPlaced(id)`, the path a recycle takes; `syncPlacedPortals` plays the fade). The contact is judged in `Tick` from the knight's circle and the player's capsule (`Impacts::ShapeOf`/`Between`, within minions.json `contact.touch_units`) on the not-touching to touching edge. A blast's grabbed knights go into `Fire::State::minionsAlight`; a stone's crush is the layer's: after the step it reads the impact watch's stone begins, takes the knights above `crush.hit_above` through `Game::Crush`, and shakes and sounds on the same contact. The layer draws a knight's shot from three effects by `Minions::EnemyShot` id (`EffectOwner::Kind::MinionShot`, its own list beside the ghost's), steps `_projectileFrameTimer` for it, and counts its fires and ends for `enemy_shot`, `enemy_shot_ended` and the shake.

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, on the 26 levels with a rolling stone that has the callback.**
- **A rolling stone that BEGINS to touch the player at a hitIntensity above 2.5 kills him** - the original's `ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone` #107-129 sets his hp to 0, the write a death area makes: blood where he stands, the lost screen, no death sound of its own. hitIntensity is the STONE's own speed along the line from the stone's point to his, over 50 px a unit: 2.5 is 125 level units a second of the original's physics, so a stone that has fallen 40 px onto his head (the case below reads 3.33; one that fell 24 px reads 2.33) or that rolls at him at that speed kills him; a stone at rest or moving away, or one he walks into, kills nothing. The stone is untouched; its shake (2 x hitIntensity) and hit sound are the row built before. The knights' crush (above 1.23) and the beholder's rocks (`Boss::Contacts`, the same 2.5, built before) are as they were.

The audit's seven (3-07, 3-10, 3-12, 3-15, 3-18, 3-20, 3-22) are only the stone levels that also place a knight.
- **Which routes.** Of the 61 that win, the ones that stand against a stone make a begin at hitIntensity 0.0 or below (1-09 twice at -0.0, 2-04 twice at 0.0, 2-07 at 0.0, 4-21 at -0.401: 2.5 and more under the kill) and 2-22, 2-31 and 3-20 make none; **none changes by a tick**. 3-12's route, which did not win before (its two knights crushed), now **dies on tick 200**: `rolling_stone_1198` begins to touch him at hitIntensity 4.28.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The callback is whole in the listing (md5 `48fe65ce` verified), the impact watch and the death funnel were built (steps 104, 142, 159). The spec's "eighth death" is stale (the knights' shot, step 159, already called itself the eighth): this is the ninth source the funnel folds in, after the hazards' own, the ghost, the boss, the turrets, the fire, the fields, the channels and the knights' shot.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`decode.md`; `docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 23's last bullet). `normal = normalize(other.GetPositionXY() - thisEntity.GetPositionXY())` (#6-26), then where `length(thisController.GetLinearVelocity()) > 0` (#28-35, else nothing at all) `hitIntensity = dp2(thisController.GetLinearVelocity(), normal) / getScale()` (#36-56), the stone's velocity and nobody else's; `isCharacter(other) && hitIntensity > 2.5f` (#106-116, strict) writes `other.SetInt('hp', 0)` (#118-127); the stone is not touched; begin-contact only (`ETHContactListener::BeginContact` runs both bodies' callbacks, `ETHContactListener.cpp:86-105`). `isCharacter` is set in one place (`GameCharacter::GameCharacter`, L22977), built by one class chain (`MainCharacter`, L24433): the player alone. `checkGameLost` (L23649 #3-116) reads hp 0 and adds `blood.ent`, hides and shrinks him and ends the game, with no sound and no shake. The callback is bound by NAME: `rolling_stone.ent` in both spellings, however it got into the level; there is no `..._rolling_stone_no_emissive`.

**WHAT IS BUILT.** `MagicPortalsLayer::stoneHits` (was `crushMinions`) reads each Stone-kind begin of the impact watch after the step, BEFORE `Game::AfterStep`: its hitIntensity is `HitIntensity(Approaching(along), along)` along the line to the other's entity point, the number the stone's own impact row and the knights' crush read; where the other is a knight above 1.23 it is crushed as before, and where it is the player `Game::StoneHitsPlayer` asks `Demolish::State::HitPlayer`, which kills above `demolish.json` `stone.kills_player_above` (strictly) and names the stone; `AfterStep` folds `demolish.playerKilled` into `Hazards::playerDied`/`killedBy` like the other eight. **A beholder's rock is not judged here**: `StoneHitsPlayer` returns false for a body in `boss.rocks`, whose kill is `Boss::Contacts`' (so 1-32 is untouched). No cue of the knights' crush is made for the player (no `minion_smashed`, no shake of 25), none of the fall's (`player_fell`); the stone's shake and `stone_hit` are the row's own.

1. **The number is the impact watch's, INFERRED equal to the callback's (STK-1; G1b-6 stays open).** hitIntensity is `Begin::Approaching(along)`: the fastest the stone came along the line since it last met or left something (at most 60 steps), over 50: the engine's solver brakes a closing pair before it meets, which Box2D's does not, so the watch recovers the speed at the START of the braking, which in a free fall is a step or two of gravity below what the original's callback would read at the touch (deviation 6, STK-9). The resting case's comment ("what it carried before is spent") and the G1b-10 case's comment (the second knight "holds beside the third crystal looking at it", so a player put on the crystals at once is in its cone) state causes that were not established: the first run's sighting was never attributed to a knight in a log (the geometry would fit the second knight, walking left past the third crystal, but nothing measured it). With Box2D's timing (BeginContact in the next step's collide with the velocity the previous step left, no speculative braking, a 0.5 px skin) the original would read 0.667, 1.333, 2.0, 2.333, 2.667, 3.0 and 4.0 for the same gaps: 0.33 to 0.67 higher. The line 2.5 is then crossed by the original at a drop over about 16 px and by the port only over about 25 to 30 px (24 px reads 2.33 and does not kill; 40 px reads 3.33 and does). Cause: the engine's speculative contact brakes the closing pair a step or two early (`Impacts.hpp`, step 152) and `Approaching()` recovers the speed at the start of the braking, not the speed gravity would have given at the touch. **No winning route has a stone begin near the threshold** (their begins on a body are at hitIntensity 0.0 or below) and the knights' crush (1.23) errs the same, strict way, so no route is thin, and 3-12's kill is 71 % over; but a route the route phase re-authors should keep any stone's begin on the player under about 1.5 until this is settled (the offset is at most 0.67, so that reads under 2.2 on the original). The offset belongs to the watch (steps 142 and 152), not to this step, which builds only the rule on its number, so the commit does not change it: **not text, left for a step of its own** (measure one stone landing on the player on the original, STK-1's capture, or settle it by arithmetic on the decoded gravity; if it holds, the stone rows read the unbraked free flight - the peak velocity plus g dt along the line for each braked step between the peak and the begin - the falls above are re-pinned and it is recorded as a gameplay change of the watch).

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`decode.md`; `derive.py`; `docs/ethanon-formats.md` section 23's last bullet). The world steps a fixed 1/30 s (`AverageFPSRateManager::AverageFPSRateManager` #1 and `manageFixedTimeStep` #3-10; `ETHPhysicsSimulator::Update`, `:154-163`), `b2World::Step` (`b2World.cpp:879-930`) finds every contact's manifold at the positions the last step left and calls `BeginContact` the first time it has a point (`b2Contact.cpp:154-229`, run at once by `ETHContactListener.cpp:86-105`), then Solves (`b2Island.cpp:206` `v += h (gravityScale gravity + invMass force)`, `:216` a damping factor of 1 - the engine never sets `linearDamping` and a stone has no `gravityScale` (`ETHEntityProperties.cpp:105`), `:298` `c += h v`; no speculative contact), so **the callback reads the velocity after the first step whose FREE position leaves the pair within its skin**: from rest `k g dt` (k / 3 in hitIntensity), the position `0.5556 k (k + 1) / 2` u. The skin is `b2CollideCircles`'s none for a circle against a circle (`b2CollideCircle.cpp:37`) and `b2_polygonRadius` (0.01 m, 0.5 screen px = 0.178 u at 720 px) for a circle against a polygon; `rolling_stone.ent` is shape 2 and the player's and a knight's `<Compound>` are two circles each, so a stone on the player or a knight is circle against circle (no TOI: both dynamic, `b2World.cpp:634-640`) and a stone on a floor circle against polygon (a static other's TOI, `:717`, reads the same velocity on the same step). **The row's figures for 2 and 6 u (0.667, 1.333) took the polygon's skin as 0.5 level units; the right figures for the player are 1.000 and 1.667, the other five agree.**

**WHAT IS BUILT.** The engine integrates a body first and brakes a closing pair after (`PhysicsSystem.cpp`: velocity and position, then `targetVelocity` capped to gap / dt for the NEXT step), in stages: a begin comes a step to eight ticks late and the history's fastest speed is one to two steps below the callback's. `Impacts::Watch` now keeps each step's centre with its velocity, and for a body marked `freeFlight` (the layer marks every rolling stone, the beholder's rocks included) that touched nothing since its history began, a begin runs `FreeFlightVelocity`: it walks the history oldest to newest, a step that moved the body as a free step does and carried another velocity on is altered at its end, and is **the other's brake** where the pair was then inside the engine's reach (the two bodies' travel in the step, the other's a step more for each since, and a slack of 1.0 level unit) and what changed was approach toward the other with no more than a friction cone's worth (1.0) of anything else - **the slack and the cone are the step's two guesses, `earthquake.json` `impacts.free_flight`, marked `_guess`**; any other alteration (a contact with something else, a gravity well, a step that left it elsewhere) is the body's own state from then on and the scan goes on; a body pushed on the step before the begin's is not replayed. From the oldest braked step the free flight is replayed one gravity step at a time (the engine's own gravity) against where the other stands, to the first step within the pair's skin (0 for two circles, `touch_px` 0.178 against a polygon) or the begin's own, and **its velocity is what `Approaching` returns** (`HistoryApproaching` is the old reading, kept, and logged beside it: `free flight read of ... : the history's X, replayed N step(s) past the brake`). It counts distance, not ticks, so a stone the staged braking parks for several ticks is read as the free flight would have been. Every reader of a stone's begin takes it through `Approaching`: the kill (`Game::StoneHitsPlayer`), the knights' crush, the stone's shake and its hit sound; `StoneHitsPlayer`, `Demolish` and `earthquake.json`'s rows are unchanged.

5. **A pair within the skin's own band (STK9-5).** The begin is found within `touch_px` (0.178 u) of any pair, as before; for two circles the original's skin is none, so a free flight whose free position stops 0 to 0.178 u short of touching is read one step early (one quantum, 0.333, low) on the begin's own step. Not hit by the table (every drop keeps 0.3 u clear of its step); a hit one time in ten of a step's travel or less.
6. **The beholder's rocks' kill is Boss's, their shake and sound are the watch's (STK9-6; STK-2 widened).** Their two estimators now differ by up to a quantum more than they did (`boss.json` `rock.crush_intensity` and `demolish.json` `stone.kills_player_above` are still equal).
7. **Not measured on the original (STK9-7; STK-1, G1b-6 stay open).** The reading is the listing's and Box2D's arithmetic checked against the port's engine, not a capture of a stone landing: no footage shows one. The replay agrees with the arithmetic in the real engine on 15 falls (nine over the player's head, four onto a floor and, since round 1, two onto a settled knight, in `test_mp_layer`; the knight is the port's one 7 px circle, so the crown the stone meets stands lower than the original's two circles of 9.1). **A reading can be LOWER than the history's** (3-14's stone on `platform_low_emissive.ent`, 2.96 to 1.12): the original's `along` is the line between the two entity points (C55), (0.94, 0.34) there, and **the history's old maximum was also a stale sample**, the stone's speed some ticks before it glanced a ramp (tick 533: its sideways speed went from +1.3 to -2.3 u a step), which no contact the watch counted cleared from the history; the callback reads the velocity AT the touch (1.0 to 1.1 along that line, the replay's 1.12). A later reader must not retune the `along` rule to the lean alone.

No route is affected (the same win ticks) and none is near a kill. Not changed in round 1: a guard would move readings on a guess, so it is recorded, and the comment of `FreeFlightVelocity` says so.

## Step 163 - a sleeper whose support is destroyed, stops being solid or is moved is woken before the step that would leave it hanging: Box2D's contact rule for every way the port removes or moves a body (built)

**GAMEPLAY: CHANGED, plainly, wherever a sleeping body rests on something the port then removes or moves**, which the census names (the 128 levels idle for 420 ticks, and the 86 route replays): a body that has been still for half a second sleeps, and until now it stayed asleep, hanging in the air, when its support went; now it falls on the tick the support goes, as in the original. The levels where a sleeper rests on something that can go or move, **by the idle census of the 128 levels and the 86 replays (a lower bound: the 42 levels with no route were looked at idle for 420 ticks only, the rule is general, and the verifier's role-based census of the same idle logs adds the exposures named after the list)**: **3-10** (knight B holds over the breakable wall; the wall breaks on tick 483 and **the knight falls from tick 484**, where it hung for 730 ticks: this moves the route, below), **2-23** (a barrel bomb on a crate that burns or blows), **2-24** (a barrel bomb on a breakable wall: woken on tick 373 in the route, which still wins on tick 471), **2-32** (a wood piece on a block the dragon's claw crushes: woken on tick 3,120; the route wins on 3,205), **4-07** (a crate on a bobbing slab: woken on tick 438 as the slab moves; the route wins on 446) and **3-12** (the stone on the small crate: as before, woken when a portal takes the crate; the route wins on 639). **The verifier's census adds, as the same exposure and not a changed behaviour of any route**: **1-30** (`level29`: `crate_small_899` asleep at tick 240 on `crate_small_900` and a platform; its stack has no remover but a portal, and the old `WakeAround` already woke a sleeper 0.09 u away) and two more pairs in 2-32 (`crate_no_emissive_ent_1161` on `double_block_plat_no_emissive_ent_1155`, and `dragon_knight` on `double_block_1288`: blocks of the dragon level, which its claw crushes). **1-09 is NOT a changing level** (this step's first text named it): the `moving_platform_single_ent_604` under its stone (asleep on tick 414 in the route replay) is a static body, the listing has `ETHCallback_moving_platform` and no `ETHCallback_moving_platform_single` (`out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce`: 0 matches; `data/entity_roles.json`), so nothing moves under that stone. Nowhere else changes **in a play the routes make**: 85 of the 86 routes win on the same ticks and the idle sweep of the 128 levels woke nothing. A play that breaks, burns, kills or moves something a sleeper rests on, in any level, is a play the old build would have hung and the new one lets fall.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** Box2D's `b2Contact`, `b2World`, `b2ContactManager` and `b2Body`, Ethanon's `ETHPhysicsEntityController` and the listing (md5 `48fe65ce`) are in hand, and the engine already offers what the rule reads (the shapes `Impacts::ShapeOf` builds, the masks, `RigidBodyComponent`'s sleep flags). The engine's `PhysicsSystem` is untouched.

**WHAT THE ORIGINAL DOES** (`docs/ethanon-formats.md`'s new bullet, which has every citation; the Box2D source under `reference/ethanon/toolkit/Source/src/box2d/`). The world sleeps (`doSleep = true`, `ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:131-132`; every body from a default `b2BodyDef`), so the original's knights, crates and stones sleep as the port's do. A destroyed body wakes what touched it: `DeleteEntity` ends in `m_world->DestroyBody` (`ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp:167-184`), which destroys every contact (`b2World.cpp:158-166`, `b2ContactManager.cpp:37-100`), and `b2Contact::Destroy` wakes both bodies of each that had manifold points (`b2Contact.cpp:101-109`), at once, inside the destroying call. A contact has points within the shapes' radii (0.01 m a polygon, none a circle against a circle) and a sensor has none (`b2Contact.cpp:173-182`). A moved body is woken itself (`SetPosXY` and its three siblings, `ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp:98-103, 136-140, 148-152, 158-162`; `b2Body::SetTransform` wakes nothing), and the sleeper beside it by the next step: `b2ContactManager::Collide` updates the contacts that have an awake non-static body (`:105-168`), which ends or changes it (`b2Contact.cpp:210-214`, or `Destroy`), and an awake body that still touches it takes it into its island (`b2World.cpp:431`). **A sleeper on a STATIC body that is moved would be left asleep by Box2D** (a contact between two bodies neither awake and non-static is not updated: read from `Collide`'s source, not run on the original), which is the likely reason the original's three scripted movers wake their neighbours themselves (the listing does not say why): `awakeEntitiesAround` (L69717) wakes every non-static body in the 3 x 3 buckets of 128 units round the mover, every frame it moves, from `ETHCallback_lift` (#321), `ETHCallback_door_lift` (#619, only when the position changes) and `ETHCallback_moving_platform` (#17).

**WHAT IS BUILT.** The engine wakes a sleeper when a contact begins with a body that is moving, or with a kinematic one (`PhysicsSystem.cpp:1080-1121`), or when the sleeper is itself written to (`:504-524`); it knows nothing of a body that is no longer there. So `Resting::Watch` does what Box2D's contact list does. The first tick it sees a loose body asleep it takes the bodies that body touches - the solid colliders whose surfaces lie within `touch_units` of it (0.5 level units) and whose masks meet its own - into a `Supports` component, with where each stood; and on every tick after, at the end of `Game::BeforeStep` (after the movers, the walls the dragon takes away and every kill and burn of the tick's `AfterStep`, before the physics step), it wakes the sleeper, and takes the component away, when one of them **is destroyed**, **is no longer solid** (a trigger now, or no collider), or **has been moved by more than `moved_m`** (1e-4 m, the engine's own `kSleepWakeDistance`) while it was not an awake loose body: an awake loose body moves by the solver, which wakes what rests on it when it stirs, so only its place is kept up to date. One rule for every way the port removes or moves a support - a wall broken, a crate burnt or blown, a door the keyhole takes, a knight killed, a lift, a door lift, a platform or a bobbing slab moved, a body a portal carries off - with no site that does so having to remember to call it. A sleeper the level places (`resting.json`) has the supports the file names for it (`rests_on`) in its component before the first look, because the port places it where the level does and the original's Box2D would have settled it onto them: 3-12's stone is 1.95 units off the crate's corner, outside any touch. `WakeAround`, which the portal calls before a traveller goes, asks the same contacts of the one body (and covers an awake body, which `Watch` does not compare). `Level::restingWoken` and `restingLooked` carry what the tick did to the layer's log: `resting: <body> asleep on tick N, resting on <support> (gap g)` and `resting: <body> woken on tick N, its support <name> destroyed | moved | no longer solid`.

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS.** (1) **`awakeEntitiesAround` is not built** (G3-6, WAKE-2): the original's three scripted movers wake every non-static body in their 3 x 3 buckets of 128 units every frame they move, touching or not; the port wakes what touches the mover (the engine's own rule keeps what touches a kinematic body awake, `PhysicsSystem.cpp:1089-1094`, and the watch wakes what rests within the touch of one outside the engine's contact margin, as it did 4-07's crate on tick 438, and what the level placed asleep against one). A scan of the placements finds a loose body in the neighbour buckets of a lift, door lift or moving platform in 26 levels (1-15, 1-16, 1-27, 1-28, 1-31; 2-06, 2-07, 2-08, 2-12, 2-15, 2-17, 2-18, 2-24, 2-25, 2-28, 2-29, 2-31; 3-05, 3-07, 3-10, 3-14, 3-15; 4-07, 4-19, 4-22, 4-31). The difference is a body that is near and does not touch, which is asleep on something else; no route shows it. (2) **A sleeper on a platform that moves** is the original's case that needs the script (a static body moved by `SetTransform`, which `Collide`'s source would leave asleep: an inference from the source, not run): the port's platforms, lifts and doors are kinematic and the engine keeps whatever touches one awake, so the case does not arise for a body in contact; **it does arise for a body that rests within `touch_units` of a mover and outside the engine's contact margin, and then it is the watch that wakes it** (4-07: `crate_ent_2161` asleep on tick 437, `resting on bounce_2107 (gap 0.0335093)`, a crate 0.03 u off the bobbing slab in a weightless room, woken on 438, `its support bounce_2107 moved`; the verifier's finding, which this paragraph had said did not arise). This step does not reproduce Box2D's bug and does not need to. (3) **The port's touch is a distance** (`touch_units`, 0.5): Box2D's is a manifold, which the port's solver does not expose; the number, like `moved_m`, is marked `_guess` in `resting.json` and measured on a plateau (above); the decoded skins are 0.178 and 0.356 at the original's 720-line screen and the port's engine rests bodies overlapping (WAKE-5). (4) **A body that arrives beside a sleeper without waking it** is not looked at: Box2D wakes both bodies of a new pair (`b2ContactManager::AddPair`, `:289-290`); the engine wakes the sleeper only when the arriving body moves, or is kinematic, and the record of what a sleeper touches is made once, when it is first seen asleep (WAKE-3); **and a sleeper first seen after its support went in the same frame is never woken** (the verifier's low, reasoned from the code and not reproduced: the frame is the engine's step, then `AfterStep`, where a wall breaks, then `BeforeStep` and the watch, so a body that dozes off in the very step before its wall breaks is first scanned with the wall already gone, records nothing to lose and hangs; not seen in the 86 replays or the 216 looks; WAKE-3). (5) **An awake loose support is the engine's**: the watch keeps its place up to date and does not wake what rests on it for a slow creep under the engine's stirring speed (0.05 m/s), where Box2D keeps the whole island awake; a body the port moves is woken for through `WakeAround` (a portal) and nothing else is (WAKE-4). **The one support a level names (`rests_on`: 3-12's small crate, 1.95 u from its stone, so no engine contact ever forms) is such a case** (the verifier's low, reasoned from the code and not reproduced; the route and the census never push the crate): the watch only refreshes an awake support's place, so an awake crate pushed off by anything but a portal (which goes through `WakeAround`) and slid away leaves the stone asleep in the air (WAKE-4). (6) **A support that is turned is not watched** (nothing in the port turns a static or kinematic body after the level is built; WAKE-6). (7) **3-10's route is not re-flown here** (the task forbids editing a route file), so the census records a level that is no longer won; the route phase of this wave re-flies it (WAKE-1). (8) The engine's `PhysicsSystem` is unchanged; the watch is the port's, which keeps the engine pin where it is and the Penumbra port's review off this step.
