## Step 165 - the pixel-centre rule for every level picture at the frame's edge: a strip of the picture's own material over the gap its edge leaves in the outer pixel, a picture that covers no pixel centre left out of the frame, from a pool made before anything else (built; verified three times, the second verification's level walk fixed and re-run, the third passing every gate row; gate 4 partial; deviation 1 of step 145 partly closed: 2-05 only)

**THE PROGRAM'S PX** (`docs/parity-backlog.md` section 6, "Step 145's recorded deviations", row 1; wave 4b, 2026-10-11, on the owner's standing order of 2026-10-10). It runs on MPR `main` at `f240af9` (the close of wave 4a), engine `710bffc`, not moved. Changed: `game/sim/EdgeCover.{hpp,cpp}` (new: the rule's arithmetic and its loader), `game/data/edge_cover.json` (new: the switches, the half pixel, the first sample, the turn and the pool, each with its source), `game/sim/CMakeLists.txt`, `game/MagicPortalsLayer.{hpp,cpp}` (`syncEdgeCovers`, `buildEdgeCoverPool`, `clearEdgeCoverLooks`, `restoreEdgeCulls`, `kEdgeCoverTag`, `EdgeCovers()`, `EdgeCulled()`), `tests/test_mp_edgecover.cpp` (new suite) and `tests/CMakeLists.txt`, three cases in `tests/test_mp_layer.cpp`, `game/LevelVisit.cpp` (round 2: the level walk's measure, below), this record, and `docs/parity-backlog.md` (the row of step 145's deviations annotated, rows PX-1 to PX-8 added). No engine change, no converter change, no route file. The evidence is under `out/parity/program/PX/` (`impl.md`; `fix1.md` and `verify1.json` for the first verification; `verify2.json`, `verify2/` and `fix2.md` for the second; `verify3.json` and `verify3/` for the third).
**GAMEPLAY: NONE.** A second quad over a gap of at most one pixel at the frame's own edge, and, for a picture that covers no pixel centre of the frame, its quad hidden for the frame and shown again before the next frame's first line of game code; nothing the simulation reads moves. The 128 route files win on exactly the ticks and shots of the last census (`R4/census_after_round1.md`): `test_mp_routes` on the fix's sources, 2,366 checks, 0 failures, 128 of 128 on the census's ticks (83 to 3,343) - the second verification's runner, the same runner re-run once in round 2 on the final text of `edge_cover.json` (`PX/fix2/suites/route_census_compare.txt`: 0 differences) - and the same through the game's own window in round 1 and again in the second verification; the third verification replayed all 128 in the runner once more and 16 of them (the ones with the most strips drawn) through the window, every one on the census's tick.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The spec's mechanism is the port's own; the engine is asked for nothing it does not do.

**THE CAUSE, as step 145 left it, and its measure on the standing baseline.** The original draws one sample a pixel at the pixel's centre; the port's engine draws 4x MSAA, so a picture whose edge lies in the frame's outer half pixel covers the edge pixel's centre and not all four of its samples (the standard positions are at 0.125, 0.375, 0.625 and 0.875 along each axis), and the pixel blends with what is behind it. On `WAKE/after/sweep/` (`MagicPortals.exe` `1c3c00a2`; two spot launches of 2-05 and 1-21 on that exe were byte-identical to it first) the edge rows that are 12 or more from the original's (RGB summed, in rows whose inner neighbour is the original's; `EC/edge_err_all.py` and `PX/tools/gate2.py`) are **777 on the left and right columns (205 on the 44 dark-sky levels, 572 on the 84 others; step 145 counted 566 on the others) and 2,210 on all four sides (260, 517, 515 and 918: left, right, top, bottom)**, and 2-05's column 1279, rows 421-586, reads **(8.9, 14.6, 16.7)** where the original's reads (1.0, 1.2, 1.3).

**THE FIX, FIRST HALF: AN EDGE STRIP** (`MagicPortalsLayer::syncEdgeCovers`, `EdgeCover::StripsOf`). One mechanism for every quad; the sky's cover (step 145) stays, and its quad is left out here. Once a frame, last in `OnUpdate` - after the engine's interpolation has written the pictures and the camera, and after `shakeView` has moved the camera, so the rectangles it reads are the ones the renderer is about to draw, at the tick's place or between two ticks, shaken or not, in a 1280 x 720 window (see WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER) - it takes every visible, upright, axis-aligned (turned by at most `turn_rad`) quad that shows something and puts its edges on the frame in pixels. An edge is **in the band** when, from the frame's side, it lies past the first sample and at most half a pixel in (a low edge in (0.125, 0.5], a high edge in [0.125, 0.5) short of the far side) **and the picture covers that pixel's centre**. Then the picture gets a strip over the gap between that edge and the frame's pixel boundary, along its own rows or columns (a top or bottom strip over the extended columns, so a corner is covered once; the long axis cut a pixel beyond the frame). The strip is a copy of the picture's whole `MaterialComponent` - taken after every tint, so its colour, light, lightmap, fade, blend and, for a flipbook, the cell the engine is about to write (`SpriteAnimationSystem::CellTransform`) are the picture's - with only `uvScale` and `uvOffset` changed: the picture's own linear uv map carried on across the gap, so the pixel's centre, where its fragment is shaded, reads the texel the picture reads there. It sits at the picture's own z and sort key, abuts the picture and never overlaps it, so a translucent picture is blended once; the picture's quad is untouched, which is why no interior pixel can move (step 145 found that widening a quad moves 4 or 5 of them). Left alone: an edge inside the frame, an edge past the pixel's centre (0.6 px), an edge that leaves every sample covered (0.1 px), a turned or mirrored quad, a hidden or alpha-0 one, a sky that has its cover. Each (picture, side) is said once in the log the frame it first has a strip (`edge strip <side> on tick N: <tag> <file> picture x.. y.. px, strip x.. y..`), 64 a level at most.

**THE FIX, SECOND HALF: THE COMPLEMENT** (`edge_cover.json` `complement`, `EdgeCover::Snap`'s inward ends, `EdgeCover::Culled`; added after the verification's first round, which found the shake half of gate 4 unmet). The first half draws out the edge that faces the frame's own side. A picture whose INWARD edge lies in the outer pixel - the black bars (z 1.0, `black_bar.ent` round the scene) that a tremble moves past the top or the bottom, a picture sliding in from a side - is the same rule seen from the other end, and the first half left it as the 4x blend: at tick 111 of 1-12's tremble the bars' inward edge was 0.394 px down, which covers two samples of row 0 and not its centre, so the port drew half a black row where the original draws none (the verification's top-row median of 0.50 at frame 111, 0.947 at 116, 0.000 at 121). The pixel-centre rule gives two cases, both inside the outer pixel and nowhere else. (1) The picture covers the pixel's centre and leaves a sample uncovered (a picture that begins outside the frame, its high edge in (0.5, 0.875] px from the side, and the mirror at the far side): the same strip, over the rest of the pixel, from the same uv map. (2) The picture's part on the frame lies wholly in one outer pixel and covers its centre nowhere (a bar's inward edge in (0, 0.5], a picture 0.3 px into the first column): the original draws none of it, a strip cannot take a sample away, so its quad is **left out of the frame for that frame** - `isVisible` false at the end of `OnUpdate` - and **shown again by the first line of the next `OnFixedUpdate` and of the next `OnUpdate`** (and by the level's unload), before any code of the game reads or writes a picture's visibility (a pooled particle is put away and brought back; `reportSprites` says what is on screen). A quad the game hid is never culled and never brought back; one it destroyed is simply gone (the layer case). What neither can take away: a picture that goes on inward from an edge in the pixel's inner half (its edge 0.5 to 0.875 px in, the picture beyond) keeps its samples of that pixel - a strip adds samples and a cull takes a whole quad - and `EdgeCover::SliversOf` names it in the log (`edge sliver <side> on tick N`), so the final comparison can attribute those pixels: 1,631 `edge sliver` lines in 113 of the 128 route logs and 206 in the sweep logs (3-16 frame 44, 3-14 frames 604-607 among them), **a residual this step does not close**. (The first verification's unattributed pixels, attributed by the second: 3-03's left column at frames 278-283 is a picture the rule culls and then gives a strip, as it says; 1-12's right columns at frames 113-114 are byte-identical with the switch off, with the first half alone and with the complement, and the log names no picture with an edge in the band there (it is silent, by design, for a turned quad and an alpha-0 one, which the rule skips), so what is shown is that the code does not move them, and they stay unattributed). The switch is `complement` (false gives round 1's draw on the same exe); `log_every_frame` (false as shipped) says every strip, cull and sliver every frame, so a capture of a pan or a tremble carries the rule's own answer for each frame.

**WHY A POOL, MADE FIRST OF ALL (the first sweep's failure).** The first build made strips on demand. Its 128-level sweep had **133 px outside the outer ring on five levels** (2-16 27, 3-21 1, 3-23 6, 4-19 87, 4-28 12), each one 5/6/5 step in one channel in the glow of an additive particle system, with the ring itself unchanged at f420. The cause, INFERRED (what was observed: the same exe is byte-identical with the switch off, and the pool removes the difference on all five levels; the gather order itself was not dumped): the renderer breaks a tie between two draws of one depth and key by the order the registry stores them in (`RenderSystem`, `gathered`), the particles of one system share both, and their glow is summed in half floats; EnTT keeps each store packed and moves the LAST entity into the place of one destroyed. A strip made late in a run is the last entity of every store, so the next particle destroyed was replaced by it and the others kept their old places: the same particles drew in another order. 2-16's `onda.png` ring wave brushes the left edge every 32 ticks, so a strip existed from tick 65 and the glow moved from tick 66; with the switch off the same exe reproduced the baseline's 2-16 byte for byte, and with the pool the first build's other four levels went with it. The pool (`edge_cover.json` `pool_size`, 24) is made hidden at attach before the camera or any other entity (`buildEdgeCoverPool`), so in the Transform and Renderable stores - the two the gather walks - every strip stands in front of every other entity, and what is made or destroyed after them moves exactly as it did before. A level that asks for more than 24 makes the rest on demand, the late way (the most first drawn on one tick of the round-1 sweeps and replays was ten, 3-21's tick 8; the second verification counted, from `log_every_frame` logs of all 128 route replays, **at most 10 strips on one tick (3-21 tick 8 and 3-15 tick 106), no tick above 24**; a seven-picture crowd in the suite asks for 28). The pool lives across levels (a retry or a skip only hides it) and goes with the layer. **The complement raises the demand** (a bar, a picture sliding in and the scene's own strips can all be drawn on one tremble frame), which `PX/fix1/tools/strips_per_tick.py` counts from the logs (`log_every_frame` true): the 10 above, so the pool of 24 was never exceeded in the 128 replays; a tick above 24 would mean the late way is live again, whatever the pixel diff says. A hidden strip is not gathered, but it is not free of the level either (next paragraph).

**THE LEVEL WALK, TWICE (the first verification's high finding, fixed in the code; the second verification's high finding, fixed in the harness).** The standing push gate - `--visit-levels lightmapped --visit-passes 2` on a copy of the gold saves - FAILED on `195f5bfa` with 259 failures, 2,010 sets and peak 128 where steps 131 and 132 recorded 134 visits, 1,460 sets, 1,100 drawn, peak 109 and 0 failures; the same exe with `enabled` false gave exactly the recorded numbers. **First cause: a hidden strip keeps what it copied.** A hidden strip keeps the `MaterialComponent` it copied, so after a level unloads it still names that level's lightmaps (the albedo, normal, orm, overlay and gloss paths of the last picture it drew). The layer invalidates a level's lightmap paths at unload (`releaseLightmaps`), and the renderer re-resolves every entity whose texture generation moved, hidden or not, so a hidden strip loaded the lightmap again and held a material set for it: the next level then "drew" the last one's lightmaps (the first failure, "level5: the sprites draw 13 lightmap(s), the level names 10", is 1-5's three lightmapped pictures, `STONE03A4x10`, `arch_with_base_blur` and `wall_w3`, held by strips) and its unload gave back fewer sets than it was told ("moved the cache from 53 to 43"). **The fix:** the level's unload clears every strip's material (`clearEdgeCoverLooks`: all of it, the five texture paths and the shared-asset path among it), the pool's entities untouched, so a strip is rewritten whole from its picture the next frame it is used and the pool stays first in the stores. The layer case pins it (a strip wearing a lightmap and a gloss map is drawn; the level is left; no strip names a texture and the pool is the same size and still first in both stores). **Second cause, found by the second verification on `cc61dd0f` (the fix's sources, the walk's first run on them): 4 failures, rc 1, the same counts (134 / 1,460 / 1,100 / peak 109) - 3-14's `lightmaps/level13b/add1468.png` and `add1469.png` "did not load", once a pass; the same four with `complement` false, none with `enabled` false.** At that level's tick 389 a strip of `wall_w3` (a lightmapped picture) is first drawn: `syncEdgeCovers` copies the picture's whole material, the overlay path among it, in the frame's `OnUpdate`, and `RenderSystem::SyncResources` gives the strip its texture ids afterwards in the same frame (`SupersonicApp.cpp` runs the layers' update at line 1647 and the resource sync at 1834; `ResourceSignature` mixes all five paths, `RenderSystem.cpp` 281-330, so the strip's changed path re-resolves it). `LevelVisit::measure` is itself a layer's `OnUpdate`, so on the one frame it runs between the two it reads a strip that names a lightmap and whose overlay id is still the black texture, and says "did not load". It is a same-frame lag in the harness, not a texture that fails to load: the frame's draw comes after the sync (and the walk's counts, which read the pictures' own sets, were right). **The fix:** `LevelVisit::measure` still puts a strip's overlay path into the set of lightmaps drawn - a strip that kept the PREVIOUS level's lightmap is exactly what the line "the sprites draw N lightmap(s), the level names M" caught in round 1, and a blanket skip would blind the gate to it - but does not read the strip's own ids or material set, which are its picture's and are read through the picture (`MagicPortalsLayer::kEdgeCoverTag`). Nothing else of the walk, the game or the pictures changes. **Re-run on `a5013ee6` (the relink of this fix; `fc70a750`, its first link, was refused by Smart App Control at its first launch): rc 0, `[LevelVisit] done: 134 visit(s), 1460 lightmap set(s), 1100 of them drawn before the measure, peak 109 in pool, 0 failure(s)`, no "did not load", no validation message, and every per-visit line of the log (cached, pool, drawn, baseline, taken) identical to the second verification's walk** (`PX/fix2/walk/visit.log`). NOT captured: the first frame a lightmapped strip is drawn (3-14's tick 6; the first frames of a level are black, its fade-in); the claim that the draw resolves in the same frame rests on the engine's order above and on the strip drawing as its neighbour row at rest (3-14 f420, row 719 against row 718: 0.986).

The first fix: 4 refusals, all of `MagicPortals.exe` on the same sources (`2de3b555`, its relinks `712358a5` and `827326a7`, and `827326a7` once more launched directly), so none of its game gates ran, until the second verification's own link `cc61dd0f` ran at its first launch and served the whole verification (0 refusals, one of its two relinks). Round 2: **1 refusal, one notification to the owner**: `fc70a750`, the first link of the harness fix, at its first launch (14:52:54, the walk, through `timeout.exe`); one delete and relink, `a5013ee6`, ran at its first launch (the walk) and for the seven launches after it; the runner `32f4a14b` ran again once. The block's own detail event (3118) in the first fix recorded a Defender cloud call and a trust value of -16777216 (read as no trust; INFERRED). The third verification: 0 refusals since 15:04 (151 launches of the game exe, 1 of the runner).

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER.**
- **Edges past the pixel's centre and edges inside the frame** stay the MSAA blends they were (the spec's own limit; step 102's note), and so does **a picture that goes on inward from an edge in the pixel's inner half** (0.5 to 0.875 px in): the complement cannot take those samples away. The log names them (`edge sliver`).
- **A flipbook that plays on its own clock** is read at the component's `frame` as the tick left it; the layer's own sheets (the player's, the shot's, the beholder's and the particles') are `playing = false` cells it sets, so the cell is exact, and no level has another.
- **A window that is not 1280 x 720**: the frame is 1280 x 720 unless a `ViewportInfo` says otherwise, and nothing in `game/` sets one (the editor does, `EditorLayer.cpp` 412 and 857), so `syncEdgeCovers` takes its 1280 x 720 fallback (`kDefaultFrameWidthPx`, "main.cpp's 1280 x 720 window") on every launch of the shipped game, as the sky's cover does. A 1600 x 900 launch on round 1 logged 1280-pixel rects while the screenshot was 1600 x 900, and so did the third verification's 1920 x 1080 launch of 2-05 ("strip x 1279.69..1280"). The strip still lands there (columns 1918 and 1919 equal, (0.99, 1.21, 1.45)), because it runs to the view's edge in metres, but the band, the first sample and the cull's outer pixel are 1280-pixel units, not the window's: at 1080p a bar's edge 0.6 real pixels in would be culled though it covers its pixel's centre. The original's comparison is at 1280 x 720, so nothing there moves. This step's earlier text ("the viewport's size", "in any window") and `edge_cover.json`'s `_about` said more than was measured and are corrected in this commit; the code's own comments already say the fallback. Never captured at another size but that one launch.

**DECODED, re-read from the listing** (`out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce`; the citations are in `lighting.json` `script_emissive._source`):

Nothing else of the listing writes the character's emissive or the door's (`blinkEmissive`'s callers, `ETHCallback_barrel_bomb`, `manageNonTeleportable`, `ETHCallback_breakable_wall` and `crateCallback`, each write their own entity; `ETHCallback_dark_dragon`, `ETHCallback_minion` and `setBackgroundTilesEmissiveColor` theirs).

The type test is the original's and the value is never read, so the port tests the key's PRESENCE, as it does for `shadowless_door`, which is the same test on all 128 levels.

**THE FIX.** `Lighting::ScriptEmissive(rules, properties, world)` returns `{ignore, door, player}`: nothing without the flag; with it, the door at `door_emissive` (0 when the level has none) and the player at `player.value` (0), or `player.lit_value` (0.2) when `world == player.lit_world` (2). The layer reads it at every level build (before the art, so a level drawn as boxes holds it, and a level without the flag does not inherit the last one's) and writes `drawn.emissive` of the door sprite and the `tint` of the player's quad; both go through the one path every sprite is lit by (`colour x min(1, ambient + emissive)`). Every number is in `lighting.json` `script_emissive` with its citation (`flag`, `door_key`, `player.value`, `player.lit_world`, `player.lit_value`): nothing is a number in code; `LoadRules` refuses a block that is missing or not what it says (names, three numbers from 0 to 1, a whole world 0 to 3).

**THE PROGRAM'S CMP3** (`docs/parity-backlog.md` section 6, "The final comparison's rows", CMP-3; wave 4c-1, 2026-10-11, on the owner's standing order of 2026-10-10). It runs on MPR `main` at `baaa651` (step 166, CMP-1), engine `710bffc`, not moved. Changed: `game/sim/Sprites.{hpp,cpp}` (`Sprite::depth`, `DrawOrder`, `Bucket`, `BucketOf`, `Standing`, `Rank`), `game/sim/Art.{hpp,cpp}` and `game/data/art.json` (the `draw_order` block), `game/MagicPortalsLayer.{hpp,cpp}` (the slots dealt when a level is built, `rankSprites` at the top of `syncSprites`, `pictureZ`), and the pins in `tests/test_mp_sprites.cpp` and `tests/test_mp_layer.cpp`. No route file, no converter file, no engine file, no `Sprites::Find` ordering change.
**GAMEPLAY: NONE.** Which of two pictures is drawn over the other; no body, shape, sensor, tick or number of the simulation reads it. Shown: the 128 route files win on EXACTLY the ticks of the last census (`R4/census_after_round1.md`), 83 to 3,343, `test_mp_routes` 2,366 checks, 0 moved; `git diff --stat` holds no file of the simulation but `sim/Sprites.*` (the picture reader) and `sim/Art.*` (the picture rules), which are presentation: `Game.cpp` and the level builder include neither, and the sim headers that include `Art.hpp` (Cutscene, Handle, Hint, Sky) take other types from it; `drawOrder` is read by the layer and the tests alone.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The renderer and the scenes read as the comparison says (below), the port already carries a slot per picture (`SlotZ`), and everything that hangs off a picture's slot (its particle systems, its light's halo) is derived from the picture's z.

**DECODED, re-read from the source.**
- The renderer keys one `std::multimap` by the draw hash, which for a type-0 entity is its z normalised over the scene's height range (`ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:68-73`, `:119-131`); equal z ties, and an equal key is inserted after its peers, so a tie is drawn in the order the entities were INSERTED. `ETHScene::MapEntitiesToBeRendered` (`ETHScene.cpp:541-576`) inserts the visible buckets one after the other, `GetIntersectingBuckets` (`ETHBucketManager.cpp:52-90`) with **y the outer loop and x the inner, both ascending**, and each bucket's list in its order. So the picture whose entity stands in the LATER bucket - the lower row, or the same row and the higher column - is drawn over the other. The bucket is `floor(position / size)` per axis (`:47-50`).
- The bucket is 128 of the level's units at any screen (`Game::start` #3-17, #44-49: `vector2(128, 128) x getScale()` as `LoadScene`'s last argument; `scaleEntities` then multiplies every entity's position by `getScale`, and none of the 128 `.esc` files carries `scalable`): `art.json` `draw_order`, cited there. It is the number `keys.json` and `minions.json` already carry; a pin reads the three equal.
- **THE RINGS OF 1-11 AND 1-12 ARE THE AGENTS' OWN PARTICLE SYSTEMS, not a z -4 antiportal and not a `shock_area`**: `anti_portal_agent_710`'s `eth_particles` (`e5e279563e11`: `onda.png`, additive, red, 1,200 ms, growth 0.8, `StartPoint` z 0) and `reflect_agent_761`'s (`ca2c812a6908`: the same wave, blue, 1,600 ms) draw at the agent's z 0 in the agent's slot; 1-11's `antiportal_709` (scale 6) is at z -6, behind every z 0 picture in both orders, so it cannot be what crossed the platform's top edge in the port's frame; neither level places a `shock_agent`, `shock_area` or `shock_diamond`. The agent stands in bucket (0, 1) over which the platform `double_block_plat_ent_708` (1, 1) is drawn, and `reflect_agent_761` (1, 1) is drawn over `wall04_ent_759` (0, 1): both are what the original's stills show (gate 2), and both are pinned through the emitter's z.

**THE FIX.** `Sprites::Rank` re-deals the slots of one `z_index` by (exact depth, bucket row, bucket column, place in the file): within each run of equal `z_index` the slots it holds go back out in that order, so the run keeps its SET of slots (a gap left by the no-portal sign stays a gap), nothing counted by `z_index` moves (the player's slot, `slotAfter`, every between-slot class of K13) and `Sprites::Find`'s order, the vector the layer walks (the crystals' and keys' phases, the sky, the emitters' stream), is untouched: only `sprite.order`, and so `drawn.z`, changes. The exact depth is `eth_z` unrounded (`Sprite::depth`): two pictures tie only at ONE depth, and level31's one node at -19.5 (z_index -20) is dealt after the -20s, as the original sorts it. The layer deals the slots at build and again at the top of `syncSprites` when any picture's bucket, read from where its entity stood after the previous tick (`ownerPx`), has changed: the original resolves a bucket move once the frame is drawn (`ETHScene.cpp:513`), so a body that crosses a line is drawn with the bucket it left for that frame and the next draw has it in the new one. What hangs off a re-dealt slot (a system that stands in its owner's slot, a light's halo) is moved by the same step; a system standing at a depth (`Slot::LiftedSystems`) does not move. A sky, its satellite and the space sky's four are pinned to the camera by the port and keep their node's bucket. Every number is in `art.json` `draw_order` (`bucket_units`, `line_tolerance_units`, with their citations); `LoadRules` refuses a block that is missing or not what it says.
**Found by the first sweep of this step, and fixed in it:** the levels put pictures exactly on the lines (x or y a multiple of 128: 1-20's `breakable_wall_ent_1061` at x 512, 2-14's `platform_no_emissive_ent_1028` at x 128, 1-11's agent at x 128, 4-16's `wall04_ent_2386` at y 128) and the original's positions are exact floats, so each is in the bucket its line opens; the port's bodies hold metres in float32 and a body that never moved reads back x 127.99999, which `floor` puts in the bucket before. The first sweep changed 48 levels but left 1-20 and 2-14 byte-identical, and 1-11 by one pixel (the right order at build, the file's order from the first tick); a temporary print of the pictures that "crossed" on the first tick listed ones at `(128.00, 240.00)` whose `atPx` printed the same. `line_tolerance_units` 0.001 (ten to a hundred times the noise) makes a position that close under a line ON it; with it the sweep below changed all 9, and that first sweep's frames were deleted (`sweep_compare_first_invalid.txt` keeps its table).

1. **The step-118 note's INSIDE-ONE-BUCKET rule is not built** (the BUILD line says to keep it and say it is not tested by the 9 pairs). The note: `scaleEntities` moves every entity to the bucket its scaled position is in, and `MoveEntity` (`ETHBucketManager.cpp:245-252`) puts a type-0 entity at the FRONT of its new bucket, so the moved ones sit in reverse file order ahead of the unmoved. The chain is also open at the engine's walk of `GetEntityArray` (a `boost::unordered_map`, so the order across load buckets is the hash's, and "reverse file order" holds only for entities of one load bucket) and at the depth normalisation's running minimum and maximum (`ETHScene.cpp:531-532`: an equal-z entity inserted after the range grew gets another depth). **BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing's callback reads as the group says (below), the port's lights are a `Light2DComponent` with a height, a range and a layer (`placeLight`), and a key's picture and entity point are in the layer's `m_sprites`.

**DECODED, re-read from the listing** (`out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce`, `ETHCallback_key` L90381, bytes 438490..442683; the citations are in `keys.json` `red_light._source`; a call pushes its last argument first, `00_order` 8.0 rule 3):
- **#119-142** `GetString('color') == 'red'` (opEquals, then `JLowZ -> 187`); **#144-149** `&& !IsHidden()` (`JLowZ -> 187`); **#151-156** `scale = GetScale().x`; **#158-186** `AddLight(GetPosition() + vector3(0, 0, 6 x scale), vector3(1, 0, 0), 48 x scale, 0)`: the bool at #158-159, the range `MULIf 48` at #160-161, the colour pushed `0, 0, 1f` (#162-166: z, y, x, so x = 1, red; read the other way it would be blue), the offset pushed `6 x scale, 0, 0` (#168-173: z first, so it is a HEIGHT).
- **Correction to step 69**: its prose and the old `_not_built` note said the offset is `(6 x scale, 0, 0)`, an x offset. The push order says z, and the colour read the same way is red. The group's text had it right.
- **What happens once the key is TAKEN**: nothing. Both jumps (`#142`, `#149`) skip only #143-186 and rejoin at #187, before the foundKeyhole branch (#204-220, the fly-in, ending in `DeleteEntity` at #646) and the ownerID branch (#653-665, a carried key); the callback calls no `Hide` and asks `IsHidden` once (#145); `Hide` is called by `scaleEntities` for the `hidden` datum and by `checkGameLost`, `checkGameEnd`, `updateEyes` and `LoadingScreen::loop`, none of them the key's file. So a key lying, carried or flying is lit, and **the light follows a carried key**: AddLight reads `GetPosition()` at the top of the call, before `linearMotion` (#666-679) and the carry's moves (#932-976), so it stands where the PREVIOUS call left the key, one tick behind its picture.
- **The engine path** (`ETHScriptWrapper.Drawing.cpp:171-183`): a script's `AddLight` makes `ETHLight(true)` with the colour, position and range as given and `staticLight = false`, and `ETHEntityRenderingManager::AddLight` (`:161-172`) keeps it unless its colour is black. It is NOT scaled by an owner (`BuildChildLight`, `:174-184`, is for a light an entity owns) and NOT multiplied by `ComputeLightIntensity` (`:111-114`, the owner's live particle share): the key's sparkles do not dim it. The shader multiplies every light by the scene's `lightIntensity` (`ETHPixelLightDiffuseSpecular.cpp:146`), and a light that is not static reaches static sprites (`ETHEntitySpriteRenderer.cpp:70`).
- **Units**: `scaleEntity` (bytes 6072..6337) #30-36 `Scale(getScale() x individualScale)` and #38-53 `SetPosition(GetPosition() x getScale())`, the z included; a key places no `scale` datum and `key.ent`'s `<Scale>` is (1, 1), so `GetScale().x` is `getScale()` and the light is 48 and 6 in the LEVEL's units (a torch's 300-unit range is drawn 300 units wide). 4-20's height over the node's eth_z: -6 + 6 = 0; 4-19's: -2 + 6 = 4.
- **The key's z is never written, so the height is the node's own** (checked at the fix round, in the callback's helpers): the only `SetPosition` with a z in them is `linearMotion`'s (`utilEntityEffect`, bytes 327527..328407, #208), `SetPosition(originalPos + offset x getScale())`, and the key's call (#666-679, the lying key only: `JNS -> 860` sends a carried key past it) passes `vertical` true (#672-673), so its offset is `(0, offset, 0)` (#151-155, pushed z, y, x), a bob in y; a carried key moves through `followUp` and `forceFollowUpPosition` and the fly-in through #576, which are all `SetPositionXY`. A carried key stands at the z it was placed at, which is what the port's light height is over.
- **Which keys**: of the 39 keys the levels place exactly two are red, level18c's `key_2701` (4-19) and level19c's `key_1335` (4-20); the boss drops are yellow (`ghost.json`, `darkdragon.json`); none carries the `hidden` datum (133 original scenes read as UTF-16: none contains the word `hidden`; `hide="0"` stands only in `level_select0-3` and `loading_screen`; no key entity has `hide="1"`, 39 keys in 133 scenes), which is why the port does not read it. `test_mp_keys` pins the census.

**THE FIX.** `keys.json` `red_light`: `colour_name` "red", `colour` (1, 0, 0), `range_units` 48, `height_units` 6, read strictly by `Keys::LoadRules` (a name, three finite channels not all zero, a positive range, a finite height). `buildLights` makes one `Light2DComponent` entity ("Magic Portals Key Light") for each drawn key whose colour is the rule's, over the key node's own depth (`Look::z`); `syncSprites` copies `drawn.ownerPx`, which still holds the previous tick's, into the light before this tick's is written (the load-time sync leaves the node's own position, the first call's); `syncLights` places it through `placeLight` with the live layer, the particle ratio 1 and owner scale 1, while the key's picture is there (placed before the shot's block, which returns). It is not the red_key_state's halo, which is an added picture of `portal_halo.png` and fades with that entity's own clock; the two are separate (no `RenderableComponent` on the light; `drawn.redKeyState` and the ambient fade are untouched).

**DECODED, re-read from the listing** (`out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce`; a call pushes its last argument first, `00_order` 8.0 rule 3; the citations are in `art.json`):
- **`ETHCallback_barrel_bomb`** (bytes 339851..340212) #1-30, unconditional, every frame: `blinkEmissive(this, GetVector3('minEmissive'), vector3(0.2), 300)`: #5 pushes the stride, #6-11 vector3(0.2) (colorB), #12-22 the datum (colorA), so the emissive runs **minEmissive -> 0.2 -> minEmissive on 300 ms legs, OVER the node's own and the .ent's 0.45**. `GetVector3` of an absent datum is (0, 0, 0) (`ETHEntity.cpp:886-890`): **15 of the 16 barrel levels blink 0 -> 0.2, so chapter 2's get brighter on average and 3-19's, 4-10's and 4-16's barrels, which carry `eth_emissive` 0.45 in the port, get DARKER**; 4-32's barrel is the one placement that carries the datum, (1, 1, 1) in `level31c.esc` id 2225 (the converter wrote the vector3 as `""`, so the port reads the key's presence and takes `floor_present`), and the dark dragon's restock sets the same on every barrel it adds (`darkdragon.json`, ins 1038-1063). `barrel_bomb_low_emissive.ent`, the ghost's restock, has no callback and does not blink. 31 placements on 16 levels, none static.
- **`ETHCallback_breakable_wall`** (bytes 347658..348349) #87-151: for a wall whose uint `blink` is not 0, `blinkColor(this, V3_ONE, vector3(0.8), 300)` and `blinkEmissive(this, V3_ONE, vector3(0.8), 300)`: colour and emissive both 1 -> 0.8 -> 1. **Both calls `AddToUInt('blinkElapsedTime', the frame's time)` on the SAME entity uint, so the wall's clock gains two frames a frame**: with `a` the level's age and `f` the frame, the colour reads `2a - f` ms (after its own add) and the emissive `2a` (after both). The entity's scale draws **its picture, its own light and its halo**: `BuildChildLight` takes the light's offset and range x scale.y (`ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:174-183`), `DrawHalo` the halo's size x scale at the unscaled position (`ETHRenderEntity.cpp:376-386`); `SetScale` leaves the particle systems (`ETHEntity.cpp:601-608`, the loop is commented out), so the flames do not pulse. 22 placements on 20 levels.

**THE CHANGE.** `art.json`: `barrel_bomb` (entity, datum, `floor_absent` (0, 0, 0), `floor_present` (1, 1, 1), `emissive.to` 0.2, 300 ms), `breakable_wall` (entity, datum, colour and emissive from 1 to 0.8, 300 ms, `calls_per_frame` 2), `non_teleportable.teleportable_emissive` (0.2 -> 0, 600 ms, `blink_datum`), `fire_agent.pulse` (1.02 -> 0.98, 300 ms); `Art::LoadRules` refuses the file without each (`barrel_bomb needs`, `breakable_wall needs`, `non_teleportable needs`, `fire_agent needs`). The layer: `buildSprites` marks a placement by its callback's name (the entity less its `.ent`, so both spellings); `syncLighting` writes a barrel's emissive from `Art::BarrelBomb::Triangle(floor)` at `age - born`, a wall's colour at `ClockMs(.., 1)` and its emissive at `ClockMs(.., 2)` over the node's own, a teleportable crate's emissive from `teleportableEmissive` through the same burnt latch the non-teleportable crate has; `syncSprites` multiplies a fire agent's picture by `fireAgent.pulse.ScaleAt(age)`; `syncLights` passes the same pulse as the owner scale of the agent's placed light (`Lighting::OwnerScaled`: range and offset x scale.y, halo size x scale). A barrel a restock adds is a copy of the placed one's sprite with `blinkBornMs` the tick it is made and the floor (1, 1, 1). The clocks are the level's age, the script's 16 ms a tick (step 147), as the antiportal's.

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS.**
1. **Gate 1's letter: 10 levels outside the 32 changed, and 2 of the 32 did not.** The spec builds the fire agent's pulse and also says the sweep changes only the 32; the fire agent is on 20 levels, 10 of them outside the group (the group's text lists it as "also decoded, not built" and names no level for it). Built, because the original does (the ruling), and explained one level at a time above; the pulse at f420 is 0.9965 of the picture's size, so the agent's edge pixels and the edge of its light's reach move. Left unbuilt, those 10 levels would keep a known difference. 2-32 and 3-15 are byte-identical because their one crate each is off the f420 frame. **The reading APPLIED (fix2, after the second verifier) and ACCEPTED at this commit (a delegated disposition, after the third verification; `CMP9/deviations.md`; no owner message, see the fix after the wave's first verifier, below): the scope is 42 levels, the 32 and the fire agent's 10.** The BUILD line names the pulse, the group's own cause text lists it ("also decoded, not built") beside the three blinks, the standing ruling decides in favour of what the original does, and splitting the pulse out would leave a known difference on all 20 fire-agent levels (10 of them outside the group) and cost a re-sweep and two relinks. **At f420, where the pulse stands at 0.9965 of the size (its ends are 0.98 and 1.02, so other phases move more, and no other tick was swept)**, the pulse changes those 10 levels little: the whole frame's mean absolute difference to the original's h6.3 still moves by 0.006 grey or less on each (`fix2/sweep_compare.txt`: 2-10 3.207 -> 3.207, 2-11 2.466 -> 2.472, 2-20 3.463 -> 3.461, 2-26 4.473 -> 4.478, 2-27 1.924 -> 1.924, 2-30 2.257 -> 2.255, 2-31 5.905 -> 5.906, 3-23 4.650 -> 4.654, 4-12 11.109 -> 11.106, 4-28 4.180 -> 4.178), which is what a 0.35 percent change of size predicts. It is not a gain at f420: four of the ten read 0.001 to 0.006 grey worse (2-11, 2-26, 2-31, 3-23), four 0.002 to 0.003 better (2-20, 2-30, 4-12, 4-28) and two are equal (2-10, 2-27), and over their changed pixels alone, on the third verification's estimator (`R4c1/verify3.json` problem 2: luma mean abs to h6.3, owner seed), 5 of the 10 read slightly away from the stills (2-11, 2-26, 2-27, 2-31, 3-23), 1 flat (2-10) and 4 toward (2-20, 2-30, 4-12, 4-28); the second verifier's "8 of the 10" (`R4c1/verify2.json` problem 2) did not reproduce, and a picture scaled by 0.35 percent moves edge pixels either way. 3. **The static entities' clock is the level's, from tick 1.** All 33 breakable walls and the fire agents are static=1: the original runs their callbacks only while their bucket is drawn, so its clock starts at the first frame the wall or agent is in the drawn buckets (the original's camera opens on `camera_start`, near the exit: G3-2). A barrel and a crate are bodies and run from the first frame. A restocked barrel is drawn from the tick it is added, where the original draws that frame at the .ent's own emissive and starts the blink on the next (one frame). **Follow-up (row CMP9-3):** a clip of 1-09 or 2-14 would measure a flagged wall's period and phase (the decode's 300 ms on the doubled clock stands; no footage holds a flagged wall); the bucket clock is G3-2's.

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The listing, `ETHEntity::Scale`, `ETHPhysicsEntityController::Scale` and `CreateBody` all say what the group says; the crate's datum is in the raw `.esc`.

**DECODED** (`out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt`, md5 `48fe65ce`; the Ethanon source under `reference/ethanon`):
- **`SGlobalScale::scaleEntity`** (bytes 6072..6337): `individualScale = 1` (ins 3), `CheckCustomData('scale')` and `GetFloat('scale')` replace it where the entity has the datum (ins 5-28), `ETHEntity::Scale(getScale() x it)` (ins 30-36), then `SetPosition(GetPosition() x getScale())` (ins 38-53; `getScale()` is 1 in the port's units). `scaleEntities` (6838..7228) runs it on every entity of the scene unless its `scalable` datum is 0, and no scene carries `scalable`; the other callers are `ETHCallback_adder` (the entity it adds, ins 32-39), `LoadingScreen::preLoop` and `PortalLevelSelector::preLoop` (the menus' scenes). **Nothing else in the listing names the string `scale`.**
- **`ETHEntity::Scale(float)`** (`ETHEntity.cpp:591-599`) multiplies `m_properties.scale` and the particle systems and calls the controller's `Scale`, which for a physics controller (`ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp:186-193`) is `Destroy()` and `CreateBody(entity, world)` afresh. **`CreateBody`** (`ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:65-117`) builds the shape from `box = GetCollisionBox(); box.Scale(entity->GetScale())`, and **`ETHCollisionBox::Scale`** (`ETHCollisionBox.cpp:105-111`) multiplies the box's size AND its offset, per axis; the fixture's density is the .ent's (`entity->GetDensity(idx)`), so Box2D's mass (`b2Body::ResetMassData`) is that density over the SCALED area: **the square of the scale**.
- **`crate_no_emissive.ent`**: shape 1 (box), Collision Size 58 x 58, density 0.4, friction 0.96, restitution 0.2, `<Scale>` 1; the placement (`level0a.esc` id 796) adds the datum `scale` float 0.75.

**THE CENSUS** (`out/parity/program/CMP16/census.md`, written FIRST by `census.py` over the 128 converted scenes AND the original's `.esc` and `.ent` files, and the listing): **72 nodes carry the datum in 53 levels, in the converted scenes and in the raw `.esc` alike: 64 `antiportal` (45 levels, values 1.3 to 13), 7 `antiportal.ent` (7 levels) and ONE `crate_no_emissive` (2-01, 0.75).** The nodes with a Body child and the datum are exactly one, 2-01's crate. The two `.ent` files that hold a default datum are `antiportal.ent` (2, overridden by every placement) and `beholder.ent` (0.75, shape 0, reached only through `ETHCallback_adder` on 1-32's marker `adder_715`, which `art.json` `beholder` already owns: its 0.75 is replaced by `bounce()`'s `SetScale` on its first turn). **The spec's hint is exact**: 2-01's crate is the one node this step changes, and 2-01 the one level its f420 frame can show. Which the port honoured before: the antiportals (picture `drawn.scale`, step 71; the refusal radius, `Portals.cpp:1346`); not the crate.

**THE CHANGE.** `LevelBuilder::ReadCustomScale` is the one reader (the datum, 1 where a node carries none, refused with its name where it is not a number above 0). `BuildNode` multiplies the box's size and offset, the circle's radius and offset and the hull's points and offset by it, and a material that states the original's own area (a knight's two circles) by its square, so the mass follows the area; `ShapeBoundsPx` multiplies the box a consumer reads (a lava's, a breakable's, a lift's or a minion's bounds, the drawn box), so it is the body's own (the original's script-side box, `GetCollisionBox`, `ETHEntity.cpp:314-321`, is not scaled by the entity's scale, only `CreateBody`'s is; the one node with both the datum and a body, 2-01's crate, is read by the drawn box alone: recorded deviation 6); `buildSprites` puts the datum in `drawn.scale`, the channel that already holds a script's `Scale()` (the static portal's 0.8 now multiplies it; the antiportal's `drawn.scale = 0.5 x zone.scale` is now `drawn.scale (= the node's scale) x 0.5`: the same double, so the 52 antiportal levels cannot change by construction, which the sweep is to confirm; checked statically: `no_portal_zone` names exactly the two antiportal spellings (`entity_roles.json`), `Portals::Find` makes a zone of every top-level node of that role (`Portals.cpp:1338-1349`) and nothing before that branch skips one, so each of the 71 has `drawn.zone >= 0` and takes the old product). The one place a picture's offset is not scaled by `drawn.scale` is the existing one (the picture hangs off its body's centre): the crate is a type-0 entity with pivot 0, so there is none to scale. **No number is in code**: the scale is the scene's, the identity default 1 is `scaleEntity`'s ins 3, and the datum's name is `LevelBuilder::kScaleDatum` with this decode beside it.

**GAMEPLAY: YES, and the rest of this paragraph is the whole of it.** The ten joints of the game (every instance of `seesaw`, `spinning_platform`, `motor_seesaw`: the census below) used to stand where the level places the swinging body A. The original does not: `ETHRevoluteJoint.cpp:35-44` sets A's anchor on `attachPointA x half of A's box` and B's on `attachPointB x half of B's box` and Box2D pulls the dynamic body (A, always) until the two world points meet. A's attach point is its centre in all ten, so **the body's centre starts on B's centre plus attach point B turned by B's angle**:

Eight of the ten move; 2-30 and 3-22 already meet. The body is on its point on tick 0 and stays there (within 0.0003 px over 420 ticks, idle: `test_mp_hinge`). The level's own `joint_pivot` decorations agree where they can: on the seesaws they stand on the held points (2-31 at (342, 250) against (341.96, 249.49) held and (356, 221) placed; 3-15 at (588, 184); 2-30 and 3-22 where placed and held are one), and in x on the spinning platforms (3-20 at 320 against 320 held and 322 placed; 2-28, 2-29 and 4-11 within 0.6); their y sits 8-13 u above the held point on the platforms (10-11 above the placed y on the unrotated ones: an offset of the decoration from its plank), so it says nothing about the y pulls there, and 3-19's plank is turned 90 degrees. **Through the routes: 2-31's route no longer wins (the player dies on tick 170), 3-20's route no longer wins (not won by tick 585) and 3-19's wins on tick 827 instead of 832.** 2-29's stone: the plank's first turn past 0.05 rad is tick 254 before and after, its angle at tick 260 is 0.1817 rad before and 0.1803 after, and the stone is 0.88 u farther along its roll at tick 400 (177.49 before, 176.61 after) and 1.04 u at tick 420 (160.00, 158.96): the tipping time moves by well under one tick (WT-10 / CMP-18's 125-135 px lag is not this step's and stays).

**BLOCKERS, checked first: none.** The tree matched the spec (`Hinge.cpp` said B's dropped attach point "costs nothing"; the converter wrote only A's anchor).

**DECODED.** `ETHRevoluteJoint.cpp:35-44`: `jointDef.Initialize(bodyA, bodyB, bodyA->GetWorldCenter())` sets both anchors on one point, then `:39-40` OVERWRITES them with `ComputeAnchorPosition(entityA, attachPointA)` and `ComputeAnchorPosition(entityB, attachPointB)`, each `anchorPoint x collisionBox.size x scale x 0.5` of its OWN entity (`:60-64`); `ETHJoint.cpp` `GetAttachPointInEntityA/B` (`attachPointAX/AY`, `attachPointBX/BY`, 0 when absent); `ETHPhysicsEntityController.cpp:252-298` `ResolveJoints`: `otherEntityName`, else the custom datum keyed like the joint (a `string` names it, an `int` is a scene id), the first entity in the array that matches; `ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:76`: a body's angle is `-radians` of the `.esc`'s and its position the entity's, no flip (so Box2D's own rotation `x' = c x - s y, y' = s x + c y` applies to the level's +y-down px). `ResolveJoints` runs once, from `SGlobalScale::scaleEntities` (listing bytes 6838..7228, `CALLSYS ResolveJoints`), so before the first physics step. The old comment said the dropped B "costs nothing" because Initialize puts both ends on one point; the constructor overwrites that.

**THE CENSUS** (`out/parity/program/CMP2/census.md`, `census.py`; derived from the original's own 133 `.esc` files, the four entity files that ship `<Joints>`, the 128 converted scenes and the listing): **10 joint instances in 10 levels: 2-28, 2-29, 2-30, 2-31, 3-15, 3-19, 3-20, 3-22, 4-11, 4-31. The spec's hint list is exact (census minus hint: none; hint minus census: none).** All ten are `revoluteJoint`, resolved through a `string` custom datum (`anchor`), one candidate B each (so the bucket order cannot pick another), A dynamic and B static in all ten, no motor enabled, no attach point A other than (0, 0), attach point B nonzero in all ten. The census's section 4 is the converted scenes before the re-conversion (`census_pre_conversion.md`: no key naming B) and after it.

**THE CHANGE.** *Converter:* `entity.py` reads `attachPointBX/BY`, the joint's name, `otherEntityName` and the datum's type (the custom data is now read before the collision, because a joint finds B in it); `tscn.py` finds B as `ResolveJoints` does (the first matching instance in the file's order) and writes, beside the eight `joint_*` keys, `metadata/joint_other` (B's node name) and `metadata/joint_anchor_b_x/y` (attach point B x half of **B's** box x **B's** `<Scale>`, in B's own frame, unturned). A joint whose partner is not placed writes neither and is reported skipped. *Port:* `Hinge::Find` finds B by `joint_other` (it requires the three keys: a level converted before this step is refused with "carries no attach point B ... convert it again", not read as zero; and it refuses a `joint_other` that is not the entity the datum names), puts the world point on B's centre plus attach point B turned by B's `rotation`, sets the body's transform where that point less A's own attach point (turned by A's angle) leaves it, and gives the engine's hinge `anchor` = A's attach point and `connectedAnchor` = attach point B. The engine's solver would take the same pull out over its first ticks at the joint's stiffness; the body is put there first so the first tick starts from the original's pose. **Re-conversion:** `out/levels/*.tscn` backed up to `CMP2/levels_before/` first; a fresh conversion into a staging directory is byte-identical to `out/levels` (128 files) and differs from the backup in exactly the ten joint files by exactly three added lines each, 30 lines in all (`CMP2/resume/levels_diff.txt`); `out/data/chapters.json` is the same. `test_mp_levels`: `metaStrings` 17,774 -> 17,784 (the ten `joint_other`), `metaNumbers` 80 -> 100 (the twenty `joint_anchor_b_x/y`), `metaNumbersOutsideJoints` 0.

`ETHCallback_rolling_stone` #0-44 then adds `rolling_stone_destroy.ent` at the stone's point (`effects.json`) and `DeleteEntity`s it; **#61-64** `startEarthquake(30, 200)` (the last-pushed is the first argument), inside the same arm: a slow touch does nothing at all. **The unit:** `GetLinearVelocity` is Box2D's m/s over the global scale 1 (`ETHPhysicsController.cpp:117-123`; 00_order 8.0 rule 5); `scale(1.5)` is 1.5 x `SGlobalScale.m_scaleFactor` (L158); a body's Box2D velocity is its level units a second x that factor / 50 (`ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:27`: 1 m = 50 raw px, raw px = level units x the factor); so the factor cancels and the gate is **1.5 m/s of the original's own physics = 75 level units a second** - D11_check C40 reads it the same ("75 u/s"). **When:** a begin-contact callback, called by Box2D's step when a pair first touches, inside `b2World::Step`'s contact update and so with the velocity the last step left, before the solver (`ETHContactListener.cpp:87-105`, called from `b2Contact.cpp:228`; D11_check C40). **Who sets `destroyable`:** the listing has two sites (`grep 'destroyable'`: #42 here, #202 of `ETHCallback_entity_launcher`, L69895, bytes 352675..353522): the launcher's `SetUInt('destroyable', 1)` on the entity it has just added (#200-209, `SetV4 v3, 1`), and the level's own placements (the census); `rolling_stone.ent` carries none.

**THE CHANGE.** *Demolish* (`State::Tick(registry, watch, begins)`): a breakable whose entity is a `breakable_wall` in either spelling (`demolish.json` `wall.entities`, `Breakable::wall`) is judged at the BEGIN of each (wall, stone) pair, which the port reads at up to two instants (`Contact::atMargin`, `atSkin`): **the first look**, when the pair comes within the contact margin and was not last tick (`State::touching`), by the speed the stones' watch carries (`Impacts::Watch::Carried`, then `Begin::HistoryApproaching(along the line to the wall)`: the fastest velocity it came toward the wall with since it last met or left something, which undoes the engine's speculative braking of a closing pair, as Impacts.hpp says); and **the second look** (fix 2), when the stones' watch finds the pair begun within Box2D's skin (`begins`: `Level::stoneWatch.AfterStep` of the same step, which runs before anything after the step moves or takes a body, so the wall still stands), by `Begin::Approaching`, which is the free flight's replay where the stone came through the air (every stone is watched so, `Game::WatchedStones`; the layer's impact watch reads the same contact the same way). The two are the engine's solver's braked estimates of one velocity, so **the larger judges**, over `SimRatio`, in the original's m/s, **strictly above `wall.breaks_above_m_s` = 1.5**; a second look that holds again is not a contact, one that breaks the wall the first held is; every stone that begins on the same step is read, so two stones that begin together both go and the wall goes once; a destroyable stone that broke a wall is taken after the step's contacts (a stone that begins on two walls breaks both), kept in `takenNow` with its name and place until the next Tick (so `FindStone` and the layer's latches still name it) and returned for `Forget`. A breakable that is not a wall (a carranca: its own backlog row) keeps the touch rule. *Game*: `Level::stoneWatch`, an `Impacts::Watch` of the level's stones (`Game::WatchedStones`: each a free flight, at 1 / SimRatio), driven from the end of `BeforeStep` and the top of `AfterStep` (the same contact skin, circle skin and free-flight judgments as the layer's watch, `earthquake.json`'s `impacts` block, now read into `Data::earthquake`; its begins go to `Demolish::State::Tick`), so a suite with no layer reads the same speed the game does; a thrown stone is `destroyable` from `launchers.json` (`destroyable: true`, #200-209). *Layer*: `rolling_stone_destroy` where a taken stone stood (a third caller of the despawner's and the rock's lambda), a log line per judged contact (`wall contact: <stone> begins on <wall> at <v> m/s (the gate 1.5): the wall breaks|holds[, the stone is destroyed] on tick N (first look at the margin, the history reads ...; the watch's begin reads ..., replayed N step(s) past the brake)`), and the begin's name for a taken stone.

**NOTES ON THE BUILD** (N1-N6: what the first listing of this step's deviations held that is a fact of the build and not a gate or an open item; each keeps its words).
N1. **The speed is the port's watch's reading, and it decides.** The callback reads Box2D's velocity at the begin; the port reads what its own solver left, with the history rule that undoes its early braking and, for a stone that came through the air, the free flight's replay of what Box2D's step would have read (Impacts.hpp, kept for the impact rows and measured against footage there, F14 and step 162). It is INFERRED equal to the original's here, not measured: no clip shows a stone breaking a wall (C40). The readings that decide a route sit under the gate by a wide margin (0.117, 0.119, 0.470, 0.621 m/s: 1-22's second stone, 3-12, 4-21, 2-29). **3-13's stone was the knife-edge, and the first version of this step got it wrong (the round-2 verifier's finding): at the margin the history reads 1.333 m/s (89 percent of the gate; 4 ticks of the world's 10 m/s^2: a port tick is one frame of the original's 1/30 s world step, 4 x 10/30 = 1.3333, and `ScriptClock.hpp` carries the body at twice that and its gravity at four times, which the reading divides back out), but the layer's own impact watch reads the very same contact, one tick later, by the free flight's replay at 1.953 m/s along the normal, 2.000 as a whole velocity - replayed 3 steps past the engine's brake - and the wall breaks. Both readings are the engine's braked estimates, so the larger judges (the second look): 3-13's wall now breaks on tick 690, and its route wins again on its census tick.** **Whether the original's stones arrive at these walls as fast as ours is still unmeasured** (the engine's solver loses some speed at a ramp's foot: 1-09's pushed stone reads 0.697 m/s). Owner: a rig measurement of a stone rolling into a wall on the original, or the route phase's choice of a faster throw where it can.
N2. **A begin is read at the contact margin's instant** (1.0 px, `demolish.json contact`, a guess since step 6) **and at Box2D's skin's** (the watch, 0.178 level units), which comes on the same step or a later one (3-13: one tick; 1-22's second stone: four). The second look only ever breaks a wall the first held. **A trial that judged ONLY at the skin's instant (round 2, tried and dropped) flipped 1-22's first stone against wall 719 from 3.162 m/s on tick 308 (breaks) to 0.015 m/s on tick 320 (holds)**: the stone is within the margin of that wall on tick 308 at 3.162 m/s, lands on the platform at the wall's foot on tick 318 (the impact row's hit 0.68) and is within Box2D's skin of the wall only on tick 320, at a creep; the committed 1-22 route relies on this stone breaking that wall, and whether the original's stone arrives at about 3 m/s is unmeasured (N1, deviation 3), so the first look keeps the verdict every earlier measurement and the route have. No pair begins twice in any of the 128 replays and the sweep, so no hysteresis is built.
N3. **The wall's break lands on the tick the margin is reached**, as before; the stone's own impact row (`stone_impact` on the wall) is the watch's and runs whether or not the wall breaks.
N4. **Non-wall breakables are untouched** (a carranca still breaks on a stone's touch at any speed: the backlog row "A stone breaks a carranca in the port only"). No live case: the 128 converted scenes place no entity named `breakable_wall*` but `breakable_wall` (26) and `breakable_wall.ent` (7) (no `breakable_wall_no_emissive`, which has no callback of its own), and no level places a stone beside a flagged breakable that is not a wall (the carrancas' levels have no stone); a pin (`ABreakableThatIsNotAWallKeepsTheTouchRule`) holds the rule.
N5. **`Impacts.hpp`'s sentence "nothing the simulation does can change" is corrected** (fix 2: the simulation reads a Game-owned watch, `Level::stoneWatch`, to decide a wall's break; the watch writes nothing).
N6. **A walkable hand-play of 1-09 no longer finishes the level** (`Level8WithTwoShots`, above); the route (level8.json) does.

## Step 177 - the modern controls' art: Magic Rampage's control buttons are made by a tool that holds no Asantee byte, into the gitignored `reference/magic-rampage/` (built; verified in two rounds; CTL-1; PYTHON AND DOCS ONLY)

**WHY.** On 2026-10-15 the owner asked for the modernised on-screen controls "taken from Magic Rampage" in place of the original's pads, which sit flush in the screen corners, and said the buttons should reuse Magic Rampage's own. The design is `docs/planning/2026-10-15-modern-controls.md` (14 steps, CTL-1 to CTL-14; its questions Q0 to Q16 are the owner's and stay open). This is its first step, and the only one with no dependency on the game: the art's one source is another project's gitignored scratch copy of Magic Rampage 7.8.7, which that project may purge, so the tool ran first. **The owner's request is the go-ahead for local use of the art, nothing more**: `docs/permission.md` is still the unfilled placeholder and says nothing about Magic Rampage (another Asantee game), so a release package that holds the folder stays gated on his word with the rights holder (design Q2). Nothing here is committed or shipped but code.

**GAMEPLAY: none. No C++, no data file, no built binary was touched.** The game does not read this art yet (CTL-8 loads it).

**WHAT THE COMMIT HOLDS.** `tools/art/make_mr_controls.py` (code only), `tools/art/tests/test_make_mr_controls.py` (29 tests; every fixture is built inside the test, no Magic Rampage file is ever opened by a test), `docs/magic-rampage-controls.md` (names, recipes, numbers and hashes, no pixels), `docs/planning/2026-10-15-modern-controls.md` (the design, with a provenance note), two README rows, this step and the DEVLOG entry. **No image, no base64, no byte of Asantee's art.**

**WHAT THE TOOL DOES.** Reads Magic Rampage's `sprites/` from `--assets <folder>` or `--xapk <file>` (or, with neither, its own verbatim copy in `reference/magic-rampage/assets`, which `--extract` fills once, 21 sprites and `extract.json`, so the original package is needed once and no longer), and writes five 128 x 128 straight-alpha RGBA files and a `manifest.json` into `reference/magic-rampage/controls/`: `walk_left`/`walk_right` (`dpad-left/right.png`, as shipped, never resampled), `restart` (`dpad-frame.png` plus `icon-restart-64.png`, restyled as the pad's own icons are), `pause` (the frame plus two bars the tool draws: a framed square, design Q5) and `clear_portals` (the frame plus a ring with an X the tool draws: Magic Rampage has none, Q12). Each carries the solid body rect (14, 14, 114, 114) inside the 14 px soft shadow, which the layout reads its insets from. **It refuses to write anywhere git does not report ignored**, before the package is even opened; the repository root is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the current directory, never a path computed from the tool's own file; without git it refuses.

**THE GATES.** Measured by the independent verifier (round 2, `out/parity/program/CTL/CTL1/verify2.json`, `pass: true`; round 1 failed on three defects, all fixed) with `tools/parity/.venv` (Pillow 12.3.0, numpy 2.5.3, pytest 9.1.1), no executable of `build/` run, nothing built; the committer re-ran pytest and ruff from the tools' final place.

| Gate | Required | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| G1 tests, lint | at least 10 pytest tests passed; `ruff check tools/art` clean | **29 passed**, 0 skipped (`-W error::DeprecationWarning`); the 10 named by the design are present; ruff clean, with no config and with `E,F,I,UP,B` at 100 columns; a mutation check of 19 deliberate breakages, each killed |
| G2 the first run | exit 0; five 128 x 128 RGBA files; `walk_left/right` equal to their source pixel for pixel; 0 exact-magenta pixels; `manifest.json`; `--check` exit 0 | **met, with one qualification (deviation 2)**: exit 0, five files, 0 magenta, 0 colour under alpha 0, `walk_left/right` max difference 0 on every pixel with alpha above 0 (alpha, straight, premultiplied and composited); `--check` exit 0 against the original extract and against the verbatim copy |
| G3 the ignore gate | `git check-ignore -v` names the `reference/` rule; `--out docs` exits non-zero and writes nothing | **met**: `.gitignore:31:reference/` for the outputs, the manifest, a sprite and `extract.json`; `--out docs`, `tools`, `game`, `tests`, `data`, `.`, `..`, `.git/x`, `engine/x`, an outside path and two junctions: exit 1, a 17,147-file path/size/mtime snapshot unchanged; no git on PATH: exit 1 |
| G4 the hard rule | the extension grep over the staged names prints nothing; nothing from `reference/` or `out/` staged; 0 images tracked; no Asantee byte in the tool, tests or doc | **met**: see the DEVLOG entry (the grep, `git ls-files` image count 0, the pin `710bffc`); the verifier found no PNG signature, base64 or `data:` URI in the three files |

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS.**
1. **`restart` masks the icon's white ink, not its alpha**: `icon-restart-64.png` carries a dark soft shadow baked into its alpha (the alpha box is 40 x 41, the arrow itself 31 x 33), so the alpha mask sized and placed the shadow. Found on the first real run, which was deleted and redone.
2. **G2's "max difference 0" holds for every pixel that shows**, not for the bytes under alpha 0: the three source sprites carry the colour (71, 112, 76) in all 937 fully transparent pixels, and the tool makes it black, as the design's own rule ("no colour under alpha 0") requires, so a plain decode differs by 112 in RGB at those pixels and nowhere else.
3. `--extract` is on by default (`--no-extract` skips it) and copies 21 sprites (4 for the controls, 9 for the editor glyphs of CTL-11, 8 spare), into the fixed `reference/magic-rampage/assets` whatever `--out` is (round 1 put them beside `--out`, which the verifier found and which is fixed and pinned by a test).
4. `--stage editor` and `--stage all` exit 2 "not yet: CTL-11". The `--xapk` path was exercised only against a zip-in-zip the tests build: no real `.xapk` was on the machine.
5. The tool is 736 lines, the tests 634 and the doc 158 (the design said about 450, 250 and 100). The ring-with-X is concentric (the X in the ring's middle), unlike the original game's own button, so that it can be centred on the body.
6. Not run: the step's own `--xapk` against the real package, and any look at the art in the game (CTL-8). A verifier probe wrote into `reference/` (ignored) and was undone byte for byte, disclosed in its report.

**LEFT FOR THE OWNER.** Look at the five buttons (a contact sheet is at `out/parity/program/CTL/CTL1/sheet.png`, gitignored): the two as-shipped arrows read smaller than the three drawn glyphs (ink 28 x 31 against 40 x 46 and 60 x 60); the pause is a framed square (Q5) and the clear-portals glyph is drawn (Q12). The rights question (Q2) before any release package holds this folder.

**LEFT FOR LATER.** CTL-2 (the classic pointer path pinned, with its baselines), then the rest of the design; the editor glyphs are CTL-11's `--stage editor`.

## Step 178 - the classic pointer path, pinned before the controls move: seventeen layer cases and one HUD case, a claim-map digest and a HUD digest kept as data, two test seams, and the classic baselines (built; reviewed, then extended once before CTL-3 began; verified independently, PASS; CTL-2; TESTS, TWO SEAMS AND CAPTURES; no gameplay change)

**WHY.** Step 177 began the design `docs/planning/2026-10-15-modern-controls.md` (CTL-1 to CTL-14). Its first C++ step is a refactor (CTL-3: one home for the control geometry, classic as a forward), and **nothing exercised a held pad before this step**: `Hud::OnPad` was pinned as pure geometry, no case put a touch on a pad, and the three consumers that ask "is this touch on a walk pad" (the camera's `onPad`, the lift gate, the tutorial-hand gate) had no test that fails when one of them is removed (backlog 140: the lift gate is a standing "left for later"). The pins go in **before** the refactor, on the unmodified claim code, so that CTL-3's evidence is "the same cases, green on the old code and on the new".

**GAMEPLAY: none.** The only production change is two public test seams in `MagicPortalsLayer`, 18 added lines and no deleted one (`git diff --stat HEAD -- game/`: `.cpp` +13, `.hpp` +5). `Hud.*`, `LevelEnd.*`, `Camera.*` and `ui.json` are untouched (S5: the diff is empty). No data file of the game's was edited; the mutation tests read a scratch copy.

**WHAT THE COMMIT HOLDS.** `game/MagicPortalsLayer.hpp/.cpp` (`ControlAt(viewPoint)`: the shown control the claim reads at a view point, an 8-line wrapper of `controlUnderPointer`; `PlaceCameraForTest(registry, centrePx)`: the follow's centre set and the camera entity placed, no production caller); `tests/test_mp_layer.cpp` (+1,438 / -1: 17 new cases, `TestPaths()` reading the test-only `MP_TEST_PORTDATA` and saying once that it does, `--record-golden <dir>`); `tests/test_mp_hud.cpp` (+78 / -1: `ThePadRectAndHitCircleAtEverySlideAge`, the same override, said); `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (+5: `MAGICPORTALS_GOLDEN_DIR` as a per-source definition on `test_mp_layer.cpp`, the pattern of `MAGICPORTALS_ROUTES_DIR`); `tests/golden/classic_claim.json` (21 snapshots) and `tests/golden/classic_hud.json` (140 entries): FNV-1a hashes and counts, **no pixel and no Asantee byte**, recorded by `test_mp test_mp_layer --record-golden` on the unmodified claim code, which refuses to overwrite a file, and **extended once** (the 14 and 138 first recorded kept their values byte for byte: deviation 11); this Step. **No image, no base64.** The baselines are in the gitignored `out/parity/program/CTL/baseline/` and are not part of the commit.

**THE PINS, AND WHAT EACH ONE CATCHES.** Each case observes one consumer of the pad's geometry, with a control beside it, so that a mutation which removes one rule fails the case that owns it.

| `ThePadHitCircleIsStrictlyInside` | **hard-coded** 63.99 and 64.01 units from each bottom corner along the edge, up the side and on the diagonal (never read from `rules.pads.hitRadiusUnits`): inside = the pad's claim, he walks, the release fires nothing (6 probes); outside = no claim, the release fires toward where it was held (6 probes); and, claim only, **exactly 64 from each corner along the edge and up the side is off the pad** (4 probes: `(64, y)` and `(0, y - 64)` for the left, `(x - 64, y)` and `(x, y - 64)` for the right; their squared distance is exactly 4096 in doubles) | a changed radius, `<` turned `<=` (the 4 exact probes), the circle turned into a box |

## Step 179 - one home for the control geometry: `sim/Controls`, classic as a forward, and the layer asks it where it asked Hud (built; CTL-3; REFACTOR, byte-identical; no gameplay change)

**WHY.** Step 178 pinned the classic pointer path before anything moved. This is the move the design (`docs/planning/2026-10-15-modern-controls.md`, CTL-3) needed first: until now the walk pads' geometry was asked of `sim/Hud` in six places of the layer, each calling `Hud::PadRect`, `PadCorner`, `OnPad`, `PadOpacity` or `PadAlphaByte` with the same arguments (the draw, the claim, the camera's `onPad` and the lift gate that shares it, the tutorial hand's gate, the ring, the end byte), and clear-portals was told from restart and pause by the **address** of its rules (`&placement != &m_hudRules.clearPortals`). A second layout threaded through six readers leaves one behind: a pad that draws in one place and presses in another. Now they ask one module, whose classic functions **call** the Hud functions and return what those returned, so the original's arithmetic is not written a second time and cannot drift by an ulp from the one the 128 sweeps, the claim-map digest and the HUD digest were taken of.

**GAMEPLAY: none.** Byte-identical classic (G4). There is no `Style` and no modern branch: CTL-4 introduces them beside these functions, which are named `Classic...` so that nothing here claims to be style-neutral. `sim/Hud.*`, `ui.json`, `LevelEnd.*` and `Camera.*` are untouched (S5: the diff is empty).

**WHAT THE COMMIT HOLDS.** `game/sim/Controls.hpp` (112 lines) and `Controls.cpp` (107): `Id` (`Left, Right, Reset, Menu, Clear`, which is the claim order, `kClaimOrder`), `IsWalk`, `HitShape` (`Rect` or `Disc`, a half-open flag, `Contains`; the default is an empty disc, so a control not yet laid out claims nothing), `Frame {rect, hit}`, and the classic functions below; `game/sim/CMakeLists.txt` (+1: `Controls.cpp`); `game/MagicPortalsLayer.hpp` (+12 / -2) and `.cpp` (+33 / -43); `tests/test_mp_controls.cpp` (467 lines, new) and `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (+4: `add_mp_test(test_mp_controls)`, no `SKIPS_WITH_77`); this Step. **No image, no base64, no Asantee byte.** `tests/test_mp_layer.cpp`, `tests/test_mp_hud.cpp` and `tests/golden/*` are **unedited**.

| Function in `sim/Controls` | Calls | Asked by, in the layer |
|---|---|---|
| `ClassicWalkFrame(rules, Id, view, age)` | `Hud::PadRect`, `Hud::PadCorner` (the disc's centre) and `rules.pads.hitRadiusUnits` | `layOutControls`, for Left and Right: `ControlButton` gains `hit`, laid out with `rect` |
| `ClassicCornerFrame(drawn)` | nothing: the drawn rectangle, closed | `layOutControls`, for Reset, Menu and Clear, wherever the entrance or the dismissal has them |
| `ClassicPlacement`, `ClassicPlace` | the rules' three `Placement`s; `Hud::Place` | the `corner()` lambda, which now takes the control and tests `kind != Control::Clear` |
| `ClassicOnWalkControl(rules, view, age, point)` | `Hud::OnPad` for Left, then for Right | `MagicPortalsLayer::onWalkControl(viewPoint)`: the camera's `onPad` (which the lift gate reuses) and the tutorial hand's gate |
| `ClassicRingCentre` | `Hud::PadCorner` | `EmitHud`'s ring (the subtraction of half the ring's size stays in the layer, in the same order) |
| `ClassicWalkOpacity`, `ClassicWalkAlphaByte` | `Hud::PadOpacity`, `Hud::PadAlphaByte` | `layOutControls`' pad alpha; `endHud`'s byte |
| `ClassicSlideUnits` | `Hud::PadSlideUnits` | no caller in the layer yet (the slide is read through the frames); it is the module's, pinned, and CTL-4's slide test reads it |

`controlUnderPointer` now asks `button.hit.Contains(at)` for all five and nothing else; `MagicPortalsLayer::Control` is an alias of `Controls::Id` with the same five enumerators, so the suites that name `MagicPortalsLayer::Control::Left` compile unedited. `onWalkControl` reads the rules, the view and the age, **not** the controls built for the level: it is not gated by the pads being shown or their pictures being there, which is what keeps the weightless quirk (a touch resting in the corner of a weightless level still counts as on a pad) and a run with no art as they were.

**THE TESTS** (`test_mp_controls`, 10 cases, **390 checks**, pure, never skips, 4 to 13 s wall: the implementer's run took 13.4 s, the verifier's on the clean exe 4.0 s; each grid case walks about two million points of a lattice). The four the design names, then six that state literals so that the equivalences are not the only oracle:

| Case | What it pins | The mistake it names |
|---|---|---|
| `ClassicHitEqualsTheHudFunctionsEverywhere` | a quarter-unit grid over the view and 8 units round it, at 16:9, 4:3 and 2:1 and eight slide ages (0 to 5,000 ms): `HitShape::Contains` equals `Hud::OnPad` for each pad (0 differ; more than 100,000 points were on a pad) and `Rect::Contains` for each corner button at its place and shifted | the shape and Hud deciding differently at one point |
