## Step 189 - the port survives a start it cannot make and a save it cannot read or write: one atomic write for the four stores, an unreadable `scores.json` kept and its medals recovered, a profile name outside the ANSI page starts the game, one try around `main`, exit codes a launcher can read, and a log that says what the build is and how long each stage took (built; ENG-2; GAMEPLAY none; classic byte-identical)

**WHY.** The owner's request of 2026-10-16 (Step 188): apply to this game "the same thing" as the crash and performance fixes made for Penumbra. Step 188 moved the engine to `5781518`. A read-only research wave (`out/parity/program/ENG/port-own-audit.md`, `penumbra-startup-crash-save.md`) found that the port had the failure classes Penumbra's E38, E40 and E45 had closed, and this Step closes the ones that are the port's alone to close (the numbers are the audit's: PA-01 to PA-06, PA-14 and the report's F1 to F6, F14). **The first thing done was to reproduce the reported crash, before any change, from one launcher with one control** (`probe/launch.py`, `python -I` from Git Bash; same exe `7d8ceaa2`, same arguments, only the environment differs): with an ASCII `TEMP` the game exits 0 in 1.89 s; with `TEMP` and `TMP` set to a folder named `tmp_<two CJK characters>` + `C-acute` + `iri` + `c-acute` (none in Windows-1252, this machine's ANSI page) it exits **0xC0000409 after 0.16 s with no output and no log**; and with an ASCII `TEMP` but `APPDATA` set to such a folder, no `--saves`, it exits **0xC0000409 after 0.10 s**, its stdout ending at "logging to ..." (the second narrowing site, `saveDir.string()`). So the research's probe P5 was real and was the profile name, and a second site beside the one the research named exists. Cause, by reading: `std::filesystem::path::string()` throws on MSVC for a character the ANSI page lacks; every such call sat outside the one `try`, so the exception ended the process through `std::terminate`. No claim here rests on the manifest alone: the exit codes above are the before, and the same three runs on the final exe (below) are the after.

**GAMEPLAY: none.** `default_mode` stays `"classic"`; `game/data/controls.json`, `sim/Controls.hpp`, `tests/golden/*`, `ui.json`, `Hud.*`, `LevelEnd.*` and `Camera.*` are untouched (`Controls::Store::Save` is the one edit in `Controls.cpp`, its body only, below). Nothing a picture, a route or the controls depend on changed: **19 of 19 classic baseline captures md5-equal to `CTL/baseline/md5.txt`**, the six-level `--controls classic` spot **6 of 6 byte-equal to `WALL/after/sweep`**, K2 (plain `--controls modern`, frame 120) `11ffeed6...` = the owner's look, the 256 `won on tick` lines md5 `362892545baa4a7857b2e7e6a40f08db`. What changes is what happens around a run that cannot go on:

- **A start with a profile name outside the ANSI page works.** `game/MagicPortals.manifest` (on `MagicPortals.exe` alone; CMake merges it with the linker's own, `requestedExecutionLevel asInvoker` kept) asks Windows 10 version 1903 and later for `activeCodePage UTF-8`; no DPI, compatibility or other element. Read back from the built exe: `activeCodePage` and `asInvoker` present, no `dpiAware`, no `supportedOS`, absent from `test_mp.exe`. `std::filesystem::temp_directory_path` is called with the error-code overload (the throwing one ended the process when `%TEMP%` names nothing), falling back to the user data directory, the executable's folder, the working directory, in that order; when none will do, the game runs with no log and says so. The code page in force is the first log line's last word.
- **One `try` around the whole of `main`** (`RunGame` is the old body; `main` catches `std::exception` and `...`). The fatal line goes through the engine log BEFORE the file sink closes (it used to go to stderr alone), and a **player's** run, defined by a rule (`game/RunKind.hpp`, `AttendedRun`: no `--frames`, `--fixed-step`, `--screenshot*`, `--hidden`, `--record`, `--replay`, `--import-assets`, `--saves`, `--route`, `--visit-levels`, `--press`, `--hold`, `--tap`, `--drag`, `--burn-dragon`, `--place`, `--light-masks-off`), also gets a message box with the reason and the log's path. A capture or a route never opens one.
- **Exit codes.** A run whose layer reports "Could not start" (the data folder missing, an unknown `--level`: `MagicPortalsLayer::StartFailed()`, set where the line is logged) exits 1; so does a `--frames` run that did not write every PNG it was asked for (`LaunchOptions::MissingCaptures`, as the engine's own `main` does), which caught a slip of my own (a relative `--screenshot` path, written into `engine/`) as `rc=1 png=0B`. A level that merely will not load is NOT "could not start": it keeps its "not playable yet" line and its way out. Checked that nothing in the repository relies on the old exit 0: no script under `tools/` launches the exe (`play_build.bat` and `port_build.bat` only build), no suite does, and the capture harness of the CTL steps (`cap2.sh`, `validate_capture.sh`, the baseline, spot and sweep scripts, all read before this was written) passes valid levels and data only; the gitignored research probes of the ENG folder that gave a bad `--data` expected the old exit 0 and are not a gate.
- **The four stores write through one function** (`sim/Files.cpp`, `WriteAtomic`): a temporary of the call's own name beside the file; written, flushed, written through to the disk (`_commit`/`fsync`, where the platform allows) and checked AFTER the close; renamed over the file in one step, the live file never removed; the temporary removed on every failure; the last good file kept as `<file>.bak` by `scores.json`, `audio.json` and `achievements.json` and only when the file in place is a good one (a file that failed to read never replaces the last good `.bak`). `Controls::Store::Save` (Step 187's shape, which this is) takes it with no backup: every pin of Steps 185 and 187 passed unchanged (`test_mp_controls` **13,621**, the count of Step 187, 0 failures).
- **`scores.json` that does not read is never deleted or written over** (policy decided by the owner's assistant on the owner's delegation; see LEFT FOR THE OWNER 1). It is renamed `scores.json.bad-<n>` (the first free `n`; a second bad file never replaces the first copy), the medals it still holds are recovered row by row (a document that does not parse is scanned for its whole rows, so a write cut short keeps every row before the cut; a row with a field missing, a medal outside 0 to 3 or a number outside a sane range costs that row), and the store carries on from them and SAVES THEM AT ONCE; the log says so (`medals: <file> is not a scores file (<why>); kept as <file>.bad-1, 3 medal(s) recovered from it`). A file that cannot be OPENED (another program holds it) is tried three times 100 ms apart (`Scores::kOpenAttempts`, `kOpenWaitMs`), then left alone: the run keeps its medals in memory, tries again at every save and as the game ends (`OnDetach`), and merges them (the better medal of each level) when the file opens. Before this, one bad byte made the store memory-only for the session and the medals earned vanished at exit.
- **Diagnostics.** `Log::SetElapsedTimestamps(true)` after the file sink opens (`INFO +1.234s [Window] ...`; the console is not stamped); the log's first line names the build (`build: Release, engine 5781518, Windows code page 65001 (UTF-8)`; the engine commit is read at configure time and re-read when the submodule's `HEAD` moves, `game/CMakeLists.txt`) and its second the folders the run reads and writes; the last line `main` writes itself is `finished: clean` or `finished: failed`, which a run killed by a crash does not write; the previous run's log is kept as `magicportals.prev.log` (it already was; verified over two launches); `manifest.pumpEventsDuringStartup = true`, whose effect was measured (below).

The full run was **predicted** at 62 suites and 57,967 checks (57,727 + 127 + 60 + 53) and **measured by the verifier at exactly that**: 62 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed, 57,967 checks.
- `test_mp_robust`: `AWriteReplacesInOneStepAndLeavesNoTemporary` (a missing folder made on the way, the replace, an empty write, the `.bak`), `AWriteThatCannotBeDoneSaysSoAndThrowsNothing` (a file where the folder should be; the target taken by a directory holding something), **`AnOldFixedTemporaryHeldOpenDoesNotStopASaveInAnyStore`** (scores, audio, achievements: a leftover `<file>.tmp` held open by another writer does not stop the save, is not touched, and no other temporary is left), `ASaveThatCannotBePutInPlaceIsToldAndLeavesWhatWasThere`, **`ABadFileNeverReplacesTheLastGoodBackup`** (audio and achievements, a torn file and a tampered list), `ScoresKeepsTheFileBeforeEachSave`, `ADirectoryIsFoundWithoutThrowing`, `AFileIsReadWholeOrSaidNot` (including a real lock with `_wfsopen(_SH_DENYRW)` on Windows), `ABadFileIsMovedToTheFirstFreeName`, **`OnlyAPlayersRunMayOpenAMessageBox`** (19 command lines parsed by the engine's own `LaunchOptions::Parse`, plus the combination).

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS.**
1. **S9 is NOT MET, with its numbers** (above): two refusals, three links. The third link was not only a retry: it carried the one-line edit to `ReportFatal`, so `main.cpp` `ddb6efc2` is what the final exe holds and every measurement above was taken on it.
2. **A new suite, `test_mp_robust`** (62 suites), rather than more cases in `test_mp_scores`: the write, the directory and the dialog rule are not a score's. The full run's expected total is a prediction.
3. **`Controls::Store::Save` adopted the helper** (scope: only if Steps 185 and 187 stay green byte for byte). They did: `test_mp_controls` 13,621, 0 failures, the printed "a handle on the live file: the replace was refused (the old bytes stayed whole)" the same as before. It takes no backup, because its pins assert the directory holds `controls.json` alone.
4. **The stores disagree on purpose.** `scores.json` quarantines; `audio.json`, `achievements.json` and `controls.json` that do not read are written over at the next save, as before (their `.bak` follows only a file that was good). Not changed here, as the scope said.
5. **The API of `Scores::Store` changed**: `Save` is no longer `const`, and `Open` returns false whenever there is something to tell, quarantine included (`Persists()` is then true); the layer logs by `WhatOpened()`. The older pin `AnUnreadableFileIsNeverOverwritten` was reversed by design, not broken.
6. **THE EXIT CODE OF A THROW IS NOT 1. An engine gap, recorded and not worked around** (the scope: engine/ is never edited here, an engine need is recorded). When the `SupersonicApp` constructor throws (every probe of a missing Vulkan loader), the fatal line, the box and the clean `return EXIT_FAILURE` all happen, and then the process dies with 0xC0000409. By reading (so an inference, not proved): `SupersonicApp.cpp:180` starts the job system's 15 workers in the constructor; its only `Shutdown` is in the destructor (`:887`), which a throwing constructor never runs; the static pool's joinable threads then terminate the process at exit; the log of the run shows no `Workers joined.` line. It is not shown to be a regression: by reading, the old `main` caught the same exception at the same place and returned the same way (the old exe is gone, so this was not run), and the engine's own `main` has the same shape; but a player sees the box and then Windows may show its own crash report. The evidence to reread: `ROB/probe/run_throw_unattended/temp/magicportals.log` ends at the `fatal:` line with no `Workers joined.` line, where a normal run's log ends with `[JobSystem] Workers joined.` and `finished: clean` (the tail of `ROB/k2/K2_f120.log`); `probe/before_control.txt`, `before_nonascii.txt` and `before_appdata.txt` are the reproduction's evidence. The fix is the engine's: the constructor's failure path shuts the job system down. A port-side option is one line in `ReportFatal`, `Supersonic::JobSystem::Shutdown()` (idempotent: it returns at once when the pool is not running); not taken, because it is a relink and the scope names an engine need as a record. Still non-zero, which is all the gate asked for.
7. **The robustness constants are in code, not in JSON** (CLAUDE.md rule 1): three tries and 100 ms (`Scores.hpp`, with their reason), the 1,000 copies of `MoveAside` and the 100,000 bound on a world or level number. They are timeouts and sanity bounds, not gameplay; the owner may overrule.
8. **No mutation hooks.** 0 added lines with `getenv`, `_dupenv_s` or `MPH_`. **Not mutation-run:** the held-`.tmp` and the quarantine pins (the old code is not here to run; by reading, the old `Save` opened that very temporary name and its second rename was the failure, and the old `Open` returned false and left the store memory-only, which the flipped pin asserted). **No test can exist for the flush and close check**: no portable way makes a small write fail at the close, so a case would pass whatever the code did; the suite's header says so. Nor for the write-through (`_commit`/`fsync`), which cannot be seen from outside the process, nor for the dialog itself (`MessageBoxW`; the rule that opens it is tested, and the box was seen once by pid in a probe). **`main.cpp` cannot be linked into a suite either**, so the one `try`, `StartFailed()` and `MissingCaptures` feeding the exit code, the mapping of the port's flags to `DevFlags`, the manifest and the `build:` line rest on probes and not on a pin; the verifier retook them on the final exe (the exit probes, the 17-run gate, the control and non-ASCII launches, the manifest read back from the exe's bytes).
9. **No message surface for the quarantine.** The layer has none: the Notificator's card is an achievement's picture and title from the original's list, and the one label (`updateHud`) is the failure-state line ("could not start", "not playable yet"). A banner over the main menu would be a screen the original never had. The WARN is in the log and on stderr only.
10. **`MoveAside` has a race** (two processes quarantining in the same instant could choose the same `n`); not guarded, said in its comment. The live file is never at risk.
11. **The directory-for-a-lock stand-in** in the suites (`create_directories` at the file's name) relies on Windows refusing to open a directory as a file; a real lock is used where `_WIN32` is defined.
12. **The OLD exe was not run on the missing `TEMP`** (G4), and the old exits (0xC0000409) for the two profile-name runs are from the reproduction made before any change.
13. **Extra log lines the scope did not ask for**: `folders:` and `finished:`; the latter is how a crashed run is told from a clean one. Extra files in a `--saves` directory from now on: a named `--level` start that unlocks achievements leaves `achievements.json.bak` beside `achievements.json` (seen in every baseline's scratch saves: `extra: achievements.json achievements.json.bak`).

**LEFT FOR THE OWNER.**
1. **The scores policy is the assistant's decision on the owner's delegation, and the owner may veto it:** an unreadable `scores.json` is quarantined and its medals recovered, never deleted or written over, never silently abandoned. The alternative, the old rule, kept the file and lost every medal earned afterwards. If he wants the other three stores to follow (a quarantine for `controls.json`, `audio.json`, `achievements.json`), it is the same few lines in each.
2. **Nothing tells the player on screen** that a save was quarantined or could not be written; the log does (deviation 9). Where and how it would show is a product choice.
3. **A player's save folder now holds more than `scores.json`**: `.bak` files beside `scores.json`, `audio.json` and `achievements.json`, and a `scores.json.bad-<n>` after a bad file. Nothing reads them but a person.
4. **The manifest needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later** to take effect; on an earlier one the element is ignored and a profile name outside the ANSI page still cannot start the game (the log's first line says the code page, 65001 or not).
5. **The exit code of a throw out of the engine's constructor** (deviation 6) is the engine's to fix, in its repository, and the pin then moves.
6. **The optional port-side workaround for that exit code is the owner's call:** one line in `ReportFatal`, `Supersonic::JobSystem::Shutdown()` (idempotent), would make a throw exit 1 before the engine fix lands. It is a relink and was not taken (the implementer asked, the verifier agreed it is the owner's).

**LEFT FOR LATER.**
- **Not in this Step, by the scope:** the release build's absolute baked paths and the black window on missing data (PA-04, ship prep); the console-subsystem exe (PA-13); Android, Vulkan 1.1, the last-run report (no phone build); the minimised-close hang (engine, not reproduced); pausing on focus loss (a product call); the other stores' policies.
- **No box for "could not start"**: the window stays on a black frame with the reason as a label and the run now exits 1 when it is closed; a player-style box after the close was not asked for.
- **`main` does not check `ReplayDiverged()`**, which the engine's own `main` does; no port run uses `--replay` (a replay of a missing file logs "nothing was replayed" and exits 0).
- **A huge `scores.json`** is still read whole (no size cap; an absurd size is `bad_alloc`, now caught by the one `try`).
- **The `.tmp` leftovers of the OLD writers** (`scores.json.tmp`, `audio.json.tmp`, `achievements.json.tmp`, and any `*.<random>-<n>.tmp` a killed process leaves) are never swept; nothing reads them.
- **A failed backup is not reported**: `WriteAtomic` can say it (`warning`), the stores pass none.
- **`Prism.cpp:157`'s fixed `.partial` name** (audit, low) and the `while` angle wraps (`Bounce.cpp`, `Torch.cpp`) are untouched.
- **The old exe on a missing `TEMP`**, and the pump on a slow machine, were not measured (one fast machine, a warm cache).
- **`assetWatching` off for a play build** (Step 188's LEFT FOR LATER said Step 189 would carry it): not done here, the scope of this Step did not name it; it moves to Step 190 with the performance options.
- **Two small gaps the verifier found, each a relink and neither changing a gate:** (a) a failed `Save` of `scores.json` after a successful open is not retried as the game ends (`OnDetach` retries only a store that is `Waiting()`), and a quarantine whose immediate write fails leaves the recovered medals only in `scores.json.bad-<n>` until a new medal is earned (a `dirty` flag would close both); (b) `FatalContext::logPath` is set before `SetFileSink` and is not cleared when the sink fails to open, so the box would then name a log that was never written. Also `game/spike/main.cpp:514` still calls the throwing `temp_directory_path()` (the spike is a dev exe that is not built).
- **Notes from the verifier:** each store's `Save` now includes a `_commit`, so the adjustment screen of CTL-11/12 should save on release and not once per frame; `".tmp"` is a bare literal twice in `Files.cpp`, beside the named `kBackupSuffix` and `kQuarantineSuffix` (a CLAUDE.md rule 3 nit).
- **Scratch left by the new cases**: `test_mp_robust`, the refused-level case (three copies of `level1.tscn`, about 40 KB) and the saves cases leave small directories in `%TEMP%` (`supersonic-test-mp-robust`, `supersonic-test-mp-layer-refused-*`, `supersonic-test-mp-layer-saves-*`, about 60 KB in all); the implementer removed them by hand after the runs. A cleanup in the cases is a test edit and a relink.

## Step 190 - the weight the game carries for nothing is taken off where it was measured: the shadow maps at 16 px and the engine's per-frame watch of every file off for a player, three small robustness gaps closed, and four candidates measured and declined with their numbers (the sprites-only pipelines, the sprite walk, the tables read again, the first use of a sound or a texture) (built; ENG-3; GAMEPLAY none; classic byte-identical in the art view)

**WHY.** The owner's request of 2026-10-16 (Step 188): apply to this game "the same thing" as the crash and performance fixes made for Penumbra. Step 188 moved the engine to `5781518`; Step 189 closed the crash and save classes; this Step is the performance half, which Step 188 promised and Step 189 left (its LEFT FOR LATER: `assetWatching` off for a play build was not in its scope). The read-only research wave found, on this machine (AMD Radeon 780M, integrated, 60 Hz, present mode FIFO), a port that holds 60 fps and carries weight a sprite game does not use: 120 MiB of shadow maps no sprite samples (the developer's lit boxes do: item 1), a lit surface shader every sprite draw folds away (the boxes' does not), a stat of every watched file on every frame. None of it is a speed problem here and the report said so; each is a cost that matters on a weaker GPU, a phone or a long session. The rule for taking any of it: **every picture byte for byte what it was, and a measured gain on a named metric; where the only expected gain is on hardware this port has not run on, say so plainly.** Three things that Step 189's verifier left (its LEFT FOR LATER and `verify1.json` defect 3) ride on the same relink and are item 0.

**GAMEPLAY: none.** `default_mode` stays `"classic"`; `game/data/controls.json`, `sim/Controls.*`, `ui.json`, `Hud.*`, `LevelEnd.*`, `Camera.*` and `tests/golden/*` are untouched. What a player gets: a smaller GPU footprint, less CPU per frame, and an exit code of 1 where a throw ended the process with 0xC0000409. Nothing a picture, a route or the controls depend on changed: **19 of 19 classic baselines md5-equal in nine variants of the options (162 launches), the 128-level f420 sweep 128 of 128 equal in three configurations (384 launches), the four timed pictures identical in all six variants of the matrix.** The verifier retook the baselines in three sets of its own (19 of 19 each, 54 launches), the sweep once (128 of 128, flagless) and the timed pictures in every variant. **One thing a picture does show, which this Step's first draft said it did not: the developer's lit boxes (the `B` key, or a level drawn without its art) lose their shadows at 16 px (item 1, found by the verifier; LEFT FOR THE OWNER 6).** The art view, which is what a player sees, is byte for byte what it was.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**

0. **The three small gaps of Step 189.**
   - (a) **A save that failed after a good open is tried again as the game ends, and so is a quarantine whose immediate write failed.** `Scores::Store` carries `m_dirty` (set by `Record`, cleared only by a write that succeeded, reset by `Open`, held across a `Retry`'s read of a whole file) and `Dirty()` (false for a memory-only store). `OnDetach` saves when `Waiting() || Dirty()`; `Retry` alone looked only at a store that never opened. Tests: `ASaveThatFailedLeavesTheStoreAheadOfItsFileUntilOneWorks` (a directory holding a file stands at the name: the save is refused, the store stays ahead, a no-change `Record` does not clear it, the next save writes both medals) and, through the layer, `AMedalWhoseSaveFailedIsWrittenAsTheGameEnds` (level0 walked to its door with that directory in the way; `OnDetach` with the way cleared writes the file; without the `Dirty()` clause the file is not there). **No test can exist for the quarantine's own failing write**: nothing lies between the move-aside and the write that a test could make fail on every platform; the flag and the write it guards are the ones the case above pins.
   - (b) **`FatalContext::logPath` is set only after the file sink really opened.** Before: the box named a log that was never written. Probe, one launcher, the same arguments, the log file made read-only and the rotation made to fail: before (`42e2f440`) the box text ended "The details are in the log: ...\magicportals.log" and the log was untouched; after (`a0a9f233`) the box says the reason alone. `main.cpp` cannot be linked into a suite, so this rests on the probe (`PERF/probe/before_probes.txt`, `after_probes.txt`). `game/spike/main.cpp:514` still calls the throwing `temp_directory_path()`; the spike is not built and is not touched.
   - (c) **A throw out of the engine's constructor exits 1.** `ReportFatal` calls `Supersonic::JobSystem::Shutdown()` last, after the log line and the box. Read at the pin before applying it: `Shutdown` returns at once when the pool is not running (every path where the throw came before the app existed, or from inside `Run`, whose app destructor has already shut the pool down); what it drains first (`Wait`) is nothing, because every `Dispatch` on the constructor's path is followed by its `Wait` with no throw between them (`TerrainGenerator.cpp:35-83`, `ParticleSystem.cpp:75-93`; and `isGame` skips `initECS`) and nothing calls `Execute`. Measured on the same probe, same arguments: **0xC0000409 before (2 of 2: the unattended probe and the attended one with the unwritable log; Step 189's verifier saw 18 of 18), exit 1 after (9 of 9: the unattended probe 7 times, the attended one with its box once, the one with the unwritable log once)**; the unusable `--data` (a start that could not start, not a throw) is exit 1 before and after. The README's exit-code sentence changed with it.
1. **`manifest.shadowMapResolution = 16`.** The engine's own range is 0 or 16 to 4096 (`GameRuntime.cpp`, `ResolveShadowMapResolution`); the log says `Created 4 x 16x16 shadow map layer(s)` (and the cube and spot maps) where it said `4 x 2048x2048`. KEPT. Measured with Windows' per-process GPU memory counters (`work/gpumem.ps1`, level12b at 5 s, both launches of each variant the same to the tenth): dedicated usage **350.6 MiB to 157.8 MiB (-192.8)**, total committed 410.9 to 218.2; the working set unchanged (203.8 against 203.7); time to first frame 0.726 s to 0.712 s (-14 ms, ranges 0.722..0.747 and 0.706..0.715, not overlapping; the verifier's retake on the final exe, 6 launches each: median 0.736 s (0.726..0.751) to 0.716 s (0.705..0.743), **-20 ms with the two ranges overlapping by one launch**, so the first-frame gain is a few tens of milliseconds at most and is not separated from the spread). The 120 MiB of the research is the arithmetic of the sizes (4 x 16 + 12 x 4 + 2 x 4 MiB); the counter fell by 192.8 MiB, so about 73 MiB is not accounted for by the sizes. That is not explained and was not investigated (an inference only: the driver's allocation granularity, or per-layer views); the saving this Step claims is the counter's, not the arithmetic's.
   **What 16 px takes away, found by the verifier and measured both ways: the developer's lit boxes cast shadows, and now they do not.** "No sprite samples a shadow map" is true; "this port casts no shadow" (this Step's first draft, the README's and the table's prose, and the research) is true of the art view only: `makeBox` gives the boxes a `castsShadow{true}` renderable and the layer's light casts, so the boxes the `B` key draws over the art, and a level drawn without its art, are the one lit, shadow-casting draw. The engine's own condition for `shadowMapResolution` is "a game that casts no shadow - every draw unlit" (`GameRuntime.hpp:128-135`), which this port is only in its art view. (i) A level run with an EMPTY `--art` folder, `--fixed-step`, frame 120, 1280x720 (the verifier's `bin/d1.sh`):

   | view | `--shadow-maps 0` | `--shadow-maps 16` (shipped) | `--shadow-maps 16 --sprites-only on` |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | level0 | `2f841f85` (A/A: two launches equal) | `4ae88d9a`: **8 of 921,600 pixels differ** (max channel delta 8) | `cfa8e813` (= `--shadow-maps 0 --sprites-only on`): 244,312 pixels (26.5%) differ, delta 156 |
   | level12b | `c6388b18`: the boxes cast soft shadows on the red ground | `79e7ee53`: **166,165 pixels (18.0%) differ**, max delta 33; no box casts a shadow (both PNGs looked at) | `b24ab147`: 840,330 pixels (91.2%) differ, delta 156 (flat, no light) |

   (ii) The `B` key itself over the real art, the view a player can reach (`B` is bound in every run, `MagicPortalsLayer.cpp:993`). `--fixed-step` cannot press a key, so the verifier's `probe/bkey.py` ran level12b in REAL time (`--frames 330 --screenshot`, no `--fixed-step`, its own scratch TEMP and APPDATA) and posted a synthetic `B` (WM_KEYDOWN and WM_KEYUP with the scancode, 150 ms) to the game window by pid at t = 3.0 s. The press took (91.0% of the pixels differ from the run with no press). Two launches per setting, A/A identical (0 of 921,600 pixels): `--shadow-maps 0` `45dd6d59` (the boxes cast shadows), `--shadow-maps 16` `75f7bbfd` (none): **165,280 pixels (17.93%) differ, max channel delta 33.** (The pictures are under `PERF/verify1/` until the close purges them; the md5s are here.)

   So: the art view, which is every picture of the gates (19 baselines in twelve sets, the 128-level sweep, the timed pictures), differs nowhere; the developer's box view loses its shadows at 16 px, and with `--sprites-only on` it is flat (measured in view (i) only, as the README says). **Decision: keep 16.** The scope recommended it and made no product call on a developer's view; to bring the shadows back set `shadow_map_resolution` to 0 or to a size between: one edit of `game/data/engine.json`, no relink. The owner's question is LEFT FOR THE OWNER 6.
2. **`manifest.spritesOnlyScenePipelines`: built, verified byte-identical, DECLINED (the table says `false`).** The four scene pipelines get the engine's `SPRITES_ONLY` specialisation: every draw this port puts through them is unlit (a sprite, a particle, a halo), and with it on **every picture was byte for byte what it was** (the 19 baselines in the `g3_sprites` and the combined variants, the 128-level sweep 128 of 128 with it on, the S/R/W pictures). It failed the rule's second half: **no gain could be measured on this machine, and a small cost was.** From the 13 launches per variant of the matrix, the four `frag.spv` pipelines take **37 ms (35..48) to create at every warm start with it on against 31 ms (29..36) plain**; the steady CPU per frame is unchanged (the pipelines are the GPU's); time to first frame 0.734 s against 0.726 s (noise); **no GPU time was measured or can be on this 60 fps FIFO machine**. The verifier retook it on the final exe (the flag changing one setting, 6 launches each): the four `frag.spv` pipelines take **37.5 ms (36..44) on against 35.5 (33..40) off**, and from the logs of its other launches 38.5 (37..45, n=4) against 32.5 (30..38, n=18): **+2 to +6 ms at every warm start**, no gain measurable, time to first frame 0.7285 s against 0.7215 s. The "6 ms" of the README, of the table's prose and of LEFT FOR THE OWNER 2 is the top of that range. ("13 launches per variant" is the matrix this item quotes; the data hold 15 per variant with the same medians.) The one number in its favour is uncontrolled: the very first compile of the four took 315 ms (181 + 80 + 28 + 26) against 641 ms (434 + 146 + 30 + 31) for the plain ones at Step 188 (two single cold launches on different days; the driver's own cache makes a controlled cold repeat impossible without clearing the owner's). The gain the engine's author measured (an Adreno 640: a 2D menu in 75 ms instead of 117) is on hardware this port has not run on: when a phone build exists the value is one edit of `engine.json` and the pictures gate there. Written in the table, in `--help`, in the README (*Performance options* and the `B` row: the developer's lit boxes, and a level drawn without its art, draw flat with `--sprites-only on`; measured by the verifier in item 1's table: 26.5% (level0) and 91.2% (level12b) of the pixels of a level drawn without its art differ from the lit view).
3. **`manifest.assetWatching = false` for a player's run** (`AttendedRun`, `game/RunKind.hpp`, the same word that decides the message box; true for every other run so parity work keeps hot reload). KEPT. Measured as process CPU time (`GetProcessTimes`: the per-frame stat sits in no profiler zone, and a FIFO loop hides it from the wall clock) over the whole launch, three interleaved launches each, 600 frames (420 for the scrolling route): still level 2562 (2219..2891) ms to **2016 (1922..2062)**, the route 2703 (2625..2812) to **2359 (2250..2438)**, the scrolling route 1875 (1859..1875) to **1594 (1500..1641)**: **0.91, 0.57 and 0.67 ms of CPU per frame**, the ranges not overlapping in any of the three; the engine's `Watching N asset path(s)` line says 47 (level12b), 30 (level0) and **0** with it off. The verifier retook it on the final exe with the flag, three interleaved launches each: still 2438 (2406..2719) to 2094 (2000..2266) ms, **0.57 ms a frame**; scrolling 1922 (1922..1953) to 1594 (1531..1641), **0.78**; route 2672 (2609..2750) to 2266 (2219..2313), **0.68**; the ranges not overlapping in any (the figures differ from the 0.91, 0.57 and 0.67 above and are not wrong in kind; the README's 0.6 to 0.9 ms holds for both takes). The wall time of 600 frames is the same on and off, as a FIFO loop must be (the verifier, still level: 10,946 / 10,910 / 10,907 ms on against 10,918 / 10,894 / 10,916 off; the route 10,923..10,938 against 10,908..10,926; the scrolling route, 420 frames, 7,873..7,892 against 7,878..7,894): the display paces it, which is why the gain is process CPU time. One side effect, measured: the `Resource Sync` zone's median rises by 0.009 ms (0.0164 to 0.0260) with the loop that walked every material gone; by reading, the registry's cache lines that loop warmed (an inference). Nothing in the port depends on the watcher: the layer invalidates its own lightmaps itself (`unloadLevel`, through `TextureRegistry::Invalidate`), and the generated control glyphs are resolved once per run at a fixed pixel size (`resolveModernImages`). Because `AttendedRun` is now also the word for a player-style run, a developer who wants hot reload in a plain window passes `--asset-watching on` (README).
4. **The port's own per-frame costs.**
   - **PA-12, the sprite walk (`reportSprites`): measured and DECLINED.** The mechanism is built (`Paths::spriteReport`, `--sprite-report on|off`; the dropped-draw alarm and `G`'s dump are kept either way) and the shipped table leaves it ON for a player: Game Layers median 0.1514 ms on, 0.1479 off (ranges 0.1472..0.1516 and 0.1468..0.1500, overlapping; the noise floor of a zone median is about 0.004 ms), 0.1185 and 0.1188 on the scrolling route, 0.1585 and 0.1555 on the route; and in a REAL console window (`CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`, the exe being console-subsystem, so every log line is a console write; four interleaved launches each, the engine's perf log) the first second's worst frame is 214 to 219 ms with the report and 214 to 219 without (the scrolling route: 183 to 195 and 185 to 194), the later windows' game time 0.19 to 0.20 ms either way (0.17 against 0.15 to 0.18 on the scrolling route, the granularity of the log being 0.01). Nothing it costs can be told from noise.
   - **PA-11, the tables read again at the start and with every level: measured, DECLINED.** Two permanent log lines now say what it costs (`tables: read in N ms`, `<level> data read in N ms`): **59 to 78 ms (median 66.5)** for the whole chain at the start (111 launches; about 9% of the 0.7 s to the first frame; nine reads and parses of `ui.json` are inside it, the share not split), and **8 to 11 ms (median 9.4)** for each level's `Game::LoadData` (one 19 ms outlier in 111 launches). Reading `ui.json` once means changing the nine `LoadRules` of `Hud`, `Pause`, `LevelEnd`, `Popup`, `MainMenu`, `Loading`, `Credits`, `Selector` and `Dashboard`, and S5 of every Step of this series forbids touching `Hud.*`, `LevelEnd.*` and `Camera.*`: a later wave's decision, with these numbers. The verifier retook both from the logs: `tables: read in` 60.2 to 73.1 ms (median 67.7, 42 launches), `<level> data read in` 8.2 to 10.1 ms (median 8.8, 32 launches); the log prints one decimal (`67.8 ms`, `7.7 ms`), and the README now says so.
   - **PA-10, the first use of textures and sounds: measured, DECLINED.** The engine's perf log (`--perf-log 1`) on the route, with and without the sound and music switches: the level's first frame is **187 to 188 ms with sound, 113 to 114 without**: the Game Layers zone of frame 1 is **73.8 to 75.4 ms with sound against 0.8 to 1.1 without** (the level's track, `finding_wonderland_60_loop.mp3`, decoded whole at tick 0 by Media Foundation: that is the answer to how long a decode takes), and the textures take 70 to 77 ms of Resource Sync on frame 1 with **214 queue waits** (69 textures at about three each). Mid-run the first uses (the research counted 13 textures and nine sounds on this route) show as windows with 15, 15 and 6 queue waits whose worst frame is 19 to 22 ms (16.7 is a frame), with and without sound: no hitch. All of it happens under the level's black cover at tick 0. The verifier retook the start (`--perf-log 1`, route level12b): the level's first frame 187 and 198 ms with sound against 114 and 112 without; Game Layers worst 73.8 and 77.0 ms at frame 1 with sound against 1.1 and 0.8; Resource Sync worst 71.7 to 77.9 ms at frame 1 in all four, 214 queue waits. PA-12 was not retaken (the numbers above are inside the noise by this Step's own account, and the table keeps it ON). A prefetch that overlaps it with the load (a worker thread, the engine's `AudioPrefetch` idea) is bigger than a small, local, test-pinned change, and on Windows it would move a stall under a cover, not remove one.
   - **Step 188's Scene Record rise (+0.05 to +0.14 ms), handed to this Step: not found, and not claimed to be noise.** Scene Record medians on the start exe `42e2f440` (three launches each, this role): 1.095 (still), 1.095 (route) and 1.035 ms (scrolling); on the new exe with every option off: 1.039 (0.985..1.085), 1.044 and 0.952; across the six variants of the new exe the still level spans 0.990 to 1.063. Launches with identical settings spread by about 0.1 ms (`off`: 0.985 to 1.085), no option moved it in one direction, and the old exe cannot be run against the new shader, so no controlled pair can be taken. On this evidence the rise cannot be told from the zone's own spread; its cause (by reading, the changed `frag.spv` or the engine's new per-frame bookkeeping) was not found.
5. **The engine's own frame statistics, off unless asked** (`--perf-log <seconds>`: fps, median, 95th percentile, worst frame, where the frame went, the queue waits; `perfOverlay` is not wired). Nothing is on by default.
6. **The options are data** (`game/data/engine.json`, read by `sim/EngineTuning`; md5 `877de7a97d71861837b579499e36b20e`, prose only edited after the gates with the values unchanged; it was `ae87c70098bc9a517f1ece4242010a2a` while every measurement ran, see THE GATES): shadow-map size 16, sprites-only false, and per kind of run (a player's, every other) the asset watching (false, true) and the sprite report (true, true), each with the measurement that decided it; five developer flags override it for one run (`--shadow-maps`, `--sprites-only`, `--asset-watching`, `--sprite-report`, `--perf-log`), given once (twice exits 1, as `--controls` does) and parsed exactly. A table that will not read leaves the engine as it was, with a WARN; the log's third line says what the run was given (`engine options (a player's run): shadow maps 16 px, sprites-only pipelines off, asset watching off, sprite report on, perf log off`). **Declining any value is an edit of that file: no relink.** The flags are not in `DevFlags`: they change what a run costs, not who is at it.

**NOT HERE, AND WHY.**
- **`sceneSamples`** (the 4x MSAA scene target): every quad edge moves (the edge-cover strips, `game/sim/EdgeCover.*`, were built for 4x), Penumbra measured 3 to 4.5% of pixels different, and the owner decides what moves pixels. The memory it would save, by arithmetic (56 B a pixel at 4 samples against 12 at one): the scene target is **49.2 MiB at 1280x720 against 10.5 MiB**, 120 and 26 MiB at 1924x1170.
- **`DynamicResolution`, `RenderScaleControl` and Penumbra's E47:** a phone's problem; no phone build exists.
- **`AudioPrefetch` (E43):** measured above (a whole track decoded at tick 0 costs 73 to 75 ms on the game thread; sound effects decoded at their first `Play` show no visible hitch); not built.
- **`minimumVulkanMinor`:** not touched.

**RECORDED DEVIATIONS.**
1. **Sprites-only was built, measured and DECLINED, and the table says so.** The scope's item 2 named `spritesOnlyScenePipelines = true`; the rule this Step set itself (byte-identical AND a measured gain on a named metric) was not met by it on this machine, and a small cost was measured (37 ms against 31 ms to create the four pipelines at every warm start). The first draft of this Step kept it on the strength of an uncontrolled pair of cold compiles (315 ms against 641 ms, different days); a review before the close asked for a controlled number from the launch logs, and those 13 launches per variant reversed it. The sweep and baseline sets that ran with it on stay in the record as the proof that it is byte-identical; the final-table sets (`g7`, `g8`, sweeps A and B) ran with it off. Declining it is not a code change: `engine.json` says `false`, `--sprites-only on` is the way to run it, and the table is the one place that changes when a phone build exists.
2. **The measurements are of a validation-ON build** (`SUPERSONIC_ENABLE_VALIDATION=ON`, every capture's setting; no `build-play\` exists), on one machine (AMD Radeon 780M, present mode FIFO at 60 Hz): the numbers are for A/B, not a player's frame rate, and a FIFO loop cannot show GPU headroom, which is why the asset-watching gain is process CPU time and the shadow-map gain is the GPU memory counter. The before side is ONE exe (`42e2f440`), the old exe being gone after the link; the same exe's every-option-off variant (`off`) is the control on the new one and agrees with it within the spread (still level: CPU 2453 against 2562 ms, Scene Record 1.095 against 1.039 ms).
3. **The working set is the PEAK over the launch (polled every 20 ms), not "at a fixed frame".** The variants of a configuration agree to within 0.5 MiB (the still level: 203.7 to 204.1 MiB), so a fixed-frame reading would add nothing; the GPU counters are sampled 5.0 s after the start (about frame 260 of a fixed-step run).
4. **The pixel gates run unattended, and a player's configuration is reached by flags there.** `--frames` and `--fixed-step` make `AttendedRun` false, so the table's attended branch cannot be exercised by a picture: it was run as a real attended launch instead (G9's smoke), and the byte-identical gates passed the attended values as explicit flags (`--asset-watching off`, with `--sprite-report off` in the earlier sets).
5. **The first measurement script wrote into the submodule.** The first run of `work/perf.py` used relative `--saves` and `--screenshot` paths (the game makes `engine/` its working directory); it left `engine/out/parity/...` (PNGs and saves, untracked). Deleted at once, `git -C engine status --porcelain` empty before and after the rerun; `perf.py` now makes every path absolute, as CLAUDE.md says.
6. **The console runs opened console windows on the owner's desktop** (29 launches with `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`, for the sprite walk's cost in a real console), and the attended smoke two windows he could see; the probes' message boxes (3) were closed by pid by the script.
7. **The new `test_mp_tuning` is a suite of its own** (63 suites), not cases in `test_mp_robust`: the table is performance, not saves. The full run's total is a prediction made before the run and met (58,110).
8. **The shipped values are NOT pinned by a test**, on purpose: a test of "the shadow maps are 16" would turn declining one into a test edit and a relink. What is pinned: the file reads strictly, its shadow size is inside the engine's range, and every run that is not a player's keeps hot reload and the sprites' log (a rule of the Step, not a measurement).
9. **No mutation runs**: a mutation run is another link of `test_mp.exe` and another notification for the owner (Step 189 declined for the same reason). What each new case would catch is said in THE TESTS.
10. **No test for (b) or (c)**: `main.cpp` cannot be linked into a suite; they rest on the before and after probes (`PERF/probe/`), which the verifier retakes.
11. **Permanent log lines the scope did not ask for**: `engine options (...)` (the run's third line), `tables: read in N ms` and `<level> data read in N ms`. They are how PA-11 is measured and cost one clock read each. Nothing in the rig anchors on a log line of the port's (the scraped ones, "Rendered N frame(s) as requested" and "Wrote", are the engine's).
12. **`game/spike/main.cpp:514` still calls the throwing `temp_directory_path()`** (the spike is not built, as the scope said: noted, not built).
13. **The pipeline cache grew** from 512,660 to 574,800 bytes (`engine/cache/pipeline_cache.bin`, the engine's ignored scratch) because the sprites-only pipelines were compiled into it by the first launch and the sets that turn them on. It does not change what the plain pipelines load.
14. **The cold-compile pair in the table's prose is uncontrolled** and is labelled so there and in item 2.
15. **Scratch left by the new cases**: `test_mp_tuning` and the new layer case leave small directories in `%TEMP%` (`supersonic-test-mp-tuning`, `supersonic-test-mp-layer-saves-failedsave`); removed by hand after the runs. A cleanup in the cases is a test edit and a relink.
16. **Literals.** The JSON keys in `EngineTuning.cpp` and the flag names in `main.cpp` are string literals, which CLAUDE.md rule 3 would call a nit; `ScriptClock.cpp` and the other readers do the same, and changing it costs a relink for no behaviour.
17. **The scope said no A/B switch stays; five developer flags and the table stay on purpose** (`--shadow-maps`, `--sprites-only`, `--asset-watching`, `--sprite-report`, `--perf-log`: one exe, one setting changed, which is how every before and after here could be taken on one exe; the table alone keeps the A/B without them, by edit, run, edit). They are the port's usual kind of developer flag (cf. `--light-masks-off`): strictly parsed, given once, documented in `--help` and the README, not an environment read and not a mutation hook. The owner may veto the flags: removing them is a `main.cpp` edit and a relink (LEFT FOR THE OWNER 7).
18. **The first draft said the port casts no shadow; the verifier measured that it does, in the developer's box view.** The README, `engine.json` and this Step now say "the art view" where they said the port, and give the numbers (item 1); the shipped value stays 16 (LEFT FOR THE OWNER 6). No code and no gate changed.
19. **Two files were edited after the verifier ran, in prose only:** `game/data/engine.json` (md5 `ae87c700...` to `877de7a9...`, every value unchanged) and `README.md` (the shadow sentence, "2 to 6 ms", the log-line decimals, the `B` row). The edit is the verifier's own DOC-ONLY list; `json.load`, the value comparison and `test_mp_tuning` (111 checks, 0 failures) were run on the edited table; no binary was relinked, so the exes the gates ran on are the exes of the commit's sources.

**LEFT FOR THE OWNER.**
1. **The shipped values are the assistant's decision on the owner's delegation, each a line of `game/data/engine.json`, and he may veto any: the shadow maps at 16 px (GPU memory -193 MiB; nothing a player sees changes, but the developer's `B`-key boxes lose their shadows: item 6), the engine's per-frame watch of every file off for a player's run (0.6 to 0.9 ms of CPU a frame; every other run keeps hot reload).** To undo either, change the number in the file: no code, no relink.
2. **`spritesOnlyScenePipelines` is off, and the case for turning it on is a phone's** (Penumbra measured an Adreno 640 drawing a 2D menu in 75 ms instead of 117). It is byte-identical in every gate here and costs 2 to 6 ms at every warm start on this machine for no measurable gain; when a phone build exists, set it true in the file and take the pictures gate there. With it on the developer's lit boxes draw flat.
3. **`sceneSamples` (the 4x MSAA scene target) is not taken and is the owner's call**: every quad edge moves (the edge-cover strips were built for 4x), and Penumbra measured 3 to 4.5% of pixels different. What it would save, by arithmetic (56 B a pixel at 4 samples, 12 at one): 49.2 MiB at 1280x720 against 10.5 MiB, 120 against 26 MiB at 1924x1170, 443 against 95 MiB at 4K.
4. **The level's first frame takes about 187 ms on this machine, behind the black cover**: the level's track decoded whole at tick 0 (73 to 75 ms) and the first use of its textures (70 to 77 ms, 214 queue waits). A player does not see it; a slower disk or a bigger track would make the cover last longer. Prefetching it (a worker thread, the engine's `AudioPrefetch` idea) is a bigger change than this Step's scope.
5. **Nothing tells the player on screen** about any of it, as before; the log's third line says what the run was given.
6. **Is a shadow-less box view (the `B` key) acceptable with the shadow maps at 16 px?** It is 18% of the pixels of level12b's box view (165,280 of 921,600 over the real art, item 1), and nothing else a player sees. To keep the shadows set `shadow_map_resolution` back to 0 (120 MiB again) or to a size between: no code, no relink. A player sees the boxes only by pressing `B`, a developer's key.
7. **The five developer flags and the table stay, against the scope's "no switch stays"** (deviation 17). Do they stay? Removing the flags is a `main.cpp` edit and a relink; the table alone keeps the A/B.

**LEFT FOR LATER.**
